title: The Role of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Predictive Virology: Forecasting, Tracking, and Combating Viral Threats.
abstract: The escalating threat of viral pandemics, dramatically illustrated by the COVID-19 crisis, has exposed the critical shortcomings of conventional reactive virology in addressing rapidly evolving pathogens. This review introduces predictive virology (PV) as an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven discipline within broader epidemic intelligence and public health surveillance that uses advanced computational tools to forecast viral threats and accelerate countermeasure design. The current review systematically examines how AI-driven approaches ( e.g. , machine learning and deep learning) are reshaping virology by integrating vast genomic datasets, multimodal surveillance signals, and advanced computational models to anticipate viral emergence and evolution before widespread transmission occurs. Core pillars of PV discussed include zero-shot mutational fitness and antigenic escape prediction using large protein language models; multimodal early-warning systems that fuse wastewater monitoring, digital epidemiology, mobility data, and social media; neural differential equation-based transmission modeling; generative AI for de novo design of broad-spectrum antivirals and vaccines; and ecological risk assessment of zoonotic spillovers. In retrospective benchmarks against deep mutational scanning experiments and real-world epidemiological outcomes (SARS-CoV-2 variants, influenza, and other outbreaks), several AI-powered tools have demonstrated performance comparable to or exceeding traditional methods, although prospective validation at scale remains limited. Despite remarkable progress, significant challenges persist, including data bias, overfitting to historical patterns, lack of prospective validation, and limited generalizability across settings. In addition, there are concerns about mechanistic interpretability, equitable global data integration, and responsible deployment. This review also critically addresses the ethical, governance, and equity implications of deploying predictive capabilities at a global scale. By consolidating cutting-edge AI methodologies with virological insights and acknowledging current limitations, this work provides a comprehensive framework for transitioning virology from a reactive to a truly predictive discipline, ultimately strengthening global health security and pandemic preparedness.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the role of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in predictive virology, focusing on forecasting, tracking, and combating viral threats. It addresses the shortcomings of conventional reactive virology in the context of rapidly evolving pathogens, as illustrated by the COVID-19 pandemic. The central question revolves around how AI-driven approaches can reshape virology by integrating genomic datasets, surveillance signals, and computational models to anticipate viral emergence and evolution.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a systematic examination of AI-driven approaches in virology, integrating genomic datasets, multimodal surveillance signals, and advanced computational models. It includes retrospective benchmarks against deep mutational scanning experiments and real-world epidemiological outcomes. The review does not report specific databases, search dates, eligibility criteria, selection method, included-study count, meta-analysis or consensus process.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: AI-powered tools have demonstrated performance comparable to or exceeding traditional methods in retrospective benchmarks. Core pillars of predictive virology include zero-shot mutational fitness prediction, multimodal early-warning systems, neural differential equation-based transmission modeling, generative AI for antiviral and vaccine design, and ecological risk assessment of zoonotic spillovers.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Significant challenges persist, including data bias, overfitting to historical patterns, lack of prospective validation, and limited generalizability across settings. Concerns about mechanistic interpretability, equitable global data integration, and responsible deployment are also highlighted. The review does not report heterogeneity, conflicting findings, weak methods, missing populations or regions, or unresolved mechanisms.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests consolidating cutting-edge AI methodologies with virological insights to transition virology from a reactive to a predictive discipline. This aims to strengthen global health security and pandemic preparedness. Specific priorities include improving data integration, prospective validation, and addressing ethical and governance implications.

Core pillars of predictive virology include zero-shot mutational fitness prediction, multimodal early-warning systems, neural differential equation-based transmission modeling, generative AI for antiviral and vaccine design, and ecological risk assessment of zoonotic spillovers. AI-powered tools have shown performance comparable to or exceeding traditional methods in retrospective benchmarks, but challenges such as data bias, overfitting, lack of prospective validation, and limited generalizability persist. The review also addresses ethical, governance, and equity implications of deploying predictive capabilities globally. By integrating AI methodologies with virological insights, the review proposes a framework for transitioning virology from a reactive to a predictive discipline, ultimately enhancing global health security and pandemic preparedness.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述探讨了人工智能 (AI) 和机器学习在预测病毒学中的作用,重点关注预测、跟踪和对抗病毒威胁。它解决了传统反应性病毒学在病原体快速演变的背景下的缺点,如 COVID-19 大流行所表明的那样。核心问题围绕人工智能驱动的方法如何通过整合基因组数据集、监测信号和计算模型来重塑病毒学,以预测病毒的出现和进化。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对人工智能驱动的病毒学方法的系统检查,整合了基因组数据集、多模式监测信号和先进的计算模型。它包括针对深度突变扫描实验和现实世界流行病学结果的回顾性基准。该综述不报告具体数据库、检索日期、资格标准、选择方法、纳入研究计数、荟萃分析或共识过程。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在回顾性基准测试中,人工智能驱动的工具表现出与传统方法相当或超过的性能。预测病毒学的核心支柱包括零样本突变适应度预测、多模式预警系统、基于神经微分方程的传播模型、用于抗病毒和疫苗设计的生成人工智能以及人畜共患病溢出的生态风险评估。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 仍然存在重大挑战,包括数据偏差、过度拟合历史模式、缺乏前瞻性验证以及跨环境的普遍性有限。还强调了对机械可解释性、公平的全球数据集成和负责任的部署的担忧。该综述不报告异质性、相互矛盾的发现、薄弱的方法、缺失的人群或区域或未解决的机制。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该评论建议将尖端的人工智能方法与病毒学见解相结合,将病毒学从反应性学科转变为预测性学科。此举旨在加强全球卫生安全和大流行病防范。具体优先事项包括改进数据集成、前瞻性验证以及解决道德和治理影响。

abstract_zh: COVID-19 危机充分说明了病毒大流行的威胁不断升级,暴露了传统反应性病毒学在应对快速演变的病原体方面的严重缺陷。本综述介绍了预测病毒学 (PV) 作为更广泛的流行病情报和公共卫生监测中人工智能 (AI) 驱动的学科,它使用先进的计算工具来预测病毒威胁并加速对策设计。当前的综述系统地研究了人工智能驱动的方法(例如机器学习和深度学习)如何通过整合大量基因组数据集、多模式监测信号和先进的计算模型来重塑病毒学,以在广泛传播发生之前预测病毒的出现和进化。讨论的 PV 核心支柱包括使用大型蛋白质语言模型的零次突变适应度和抗原逃逸预测;融合废水监测、数字流行病学、移动数据和社交媒体的多模式预警系统;基于神经微分方程的传输建模;用于广谱抗病毒药物和疫苗从头设计的生成式人工智能;人畜共患病溢出效应的生态风险评估。在针对深度突变扫描实验和现实世界流行病学结果(SARS-CoV-2变种、流感和其他疫情)的回顾性基准中,一些人工智能驱动的工具已证明其性能可与或超过传统方法,尽管大规模的前瞻性验证仍然有限。尽管取得了显着的进展,但仍然存在重大挑战,包括数据偏差、过度拟合历史模式、缺乏前瞻性验证以及跨环境的普遍性有限。此外,人们还担心机械可解释性、公平的全球数据集成和负责任的部署。本次审查还批判性地讨论了在全球范围内部署预测能力的道德、治理和公平影响。通过将尖端人工智能方法与病毒学见解相结合并承认当前的局限性,这项工作提供了一个全面的框架,将病毒学从反应性学科转变为真正的预测性学科,最终加强全球卫生安全和大流行病的防范。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对人工智能驱动的病毒学方法的系统检查,整合了基因组数据集、多模式监测信号和先进的计算模型。它包括针对深度突变扫描实验和现实世界流行病学结果的回顾性基准。该综述不报告具体数据库、检索日期、资格标准、选择方法、纳入研究计数、荟萃分析或共识过程。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 在回顾性基准测试中,人工智能驱动的工具表现出与传统方法相当或超过的性能。预测病毒学的核心支柱包括零样本突变适应度预测、多模式预警系统、基于神经微分方程的传播模型、用于抗病毒和疫苗设计的生成人工智能以及人畜共患病溢出的生态风险评估。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 仍然存在重大挑战,包括数据偏差、过度拟合历史模式、缺乏前瞻性验证以及跨环境的普遍性有限。还强调了对机械可解释性、公平的全球数据集成和负责任的部署的担忧。该综述不报告异质性、相互矛盾的发现、薄弱的方法、缺失的人群或区域或未解决的机制。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该评论建议将尖端的人工智能方法与病毒学见解相结合,将病毒学从反应性学科转变为预测性学科。此举旨在加强全球卫生安全和大流行病防范。具体优先事项包括改进数据集成、前瞻性验证以及解决道德和治理影响。

title: Variant-specific and cross-reactive antibody responses following COVID-19 booster vaccinations and SARS-CoV-2 breakthrough infections
abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 has evolved into several genetic variants, all bearing mutations that reduce antibody binding and affect vaccine and treatment effectiveness. Updated COVID-19 vaccines, including bivalent formulations (wild type [WT]/BA.1 or WT/BA.5) and more recent monovalent versions targeting emerging variants such as XBB.1.5, JN.1, KP.2 or LP.8.1, were developed to broaden protection. However, immune imprinting may limit the induction of neutralizing antibodies against strains that differ significantly, even after receiving several variant-specific boosters. A deeper understanding of how booster vaccination reshapes antibody specificity remains essential for rational vaccine design. We examined the antibody response to a bivalent WT/BA.5 booster, focusing on antibody levels and neutralization. Serum samples collected before and after a fourth dose of monovalent WT or bivalent (WT/BA.5) mRNA vaccines were compared with sera from individuals after primary WT infections and Omicron BA.1, BA.2, or BA.5 breakthrough infections. We found that both monovalent and bivalent boosters significantly increased IgG and neutralizing antibodies, but breakthrough infections induced broader cross-reactive responses. Depletion experiments revealed that booster-induced immunity was predominantly mediated by cross-reactive antibodies, with the highest levels after breakthrough infections and the lowest after a primary WT infection. These findings provide functional insights into the antibody specificities associated with imprinting effects following variant-adapted booster vaccination.

title_zh: COVID-19 加强疫苗接种和 SARS-CoV-2 突破性感染后的变体特异性和交叉反应性抗体反应
source_body_en: Abstract SARS-CoV-2 has evolved into several genetic variants, all bearing mutations that reduce antibody binding and affect vaccine and treatment effectiveness. Updated COVID-19 vaccines, including bivalent formulations (wild type [WT]/BA.1 or WT/BA.5) and more recent monovalent versions targeting emerging variants such as XBB.1.5, JN.1, KP.2 or LP.8.1, were developed to broaden protection. However, immune imprinting may limit the induction of neutralizing antibodies against strains that differ significantly, even after receiving several variant-specific boosters. A deeper understanding of how booster vaccination reshapes antibody specificity remains essential for rational vaccine design. We examined the antibody response to a bivalent WT/BA.5 booster, focusing on antibody levels and neutralization. Serum samples collected before and after a fourth dose of monovalent WT or bivalent (WT/BA.5) mRNA vaccines were compared with sera from individuals after primary WT infections and Omicron BA.1, BA.2, or BA.5 breakthrough infections. We found that both monovalent and bivalent boosters significantly increased IgG and neutralizing antibodies, but breakthrough infections induced broader cross-reactive responses. Depletion experiments revealed that booster-induced immunity was predominantly mediated by cross-reactive antibodies, with the highest levels after breakthrough infections and the lowest after a primary WT infection. These findings provide functional insights into the antibody specificities associated with imprinting effects following variant-adapted booster vaccination.

title: Cost and Safety Perceptions as Determinants of COVID-19 Vaccination Intention in Saudi Arabia
abstract: Background: Public acceptance of vaccines during emerging infectious disease outbreaks is influenced by perceptions of safety, accessibility, and cost. Understanding these determinants during the early phase of a pandemic is important for informing vaccination policy and communication strategies. This study examined the role of vaccine cost and safety perceptions in shaping COVID-19 vaccination intention among adults in Saudi Arabia prior to national vaccine rollout. Methods: A cross-sectional electronic survey was conducted among adults residing in Saudi Arabia between August and September 2020. Participants were recruited through online distribution using social media and electronic communication channels. The questionnaire assessed socio-demographic characteristics, knowledge and perceptions regarding COVID-19, and intention to receive COVID-19 vaccination under five hypothetical scenarios reflecting vaccine cost and the availability of scientific safety and efficacy evidence. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with vaccination intention. Results: A total of 1293 respondents completed the survey. When vaccination was offered free of charge, 57.5% of participants reported that they would likely receive the vaccine. Vaccination intention declined as the hypothetical vaccine price increased, reaching 38.7% when the cost exceeded 100 SAR. Intention was lowest when vaccination was presented under conditions in which safety and efficacy evidence had not yet been confirmed. Age, gender, educational attainment, and prior seasonal influenza vaccination were associated with COVID-19 vaccination intention across several scenarios. Conclusions: Perceived vaccine affordability and confidence in scientific safety and efficacy evidence were important factors associated with COVID-19 vaccination intention during the early phase of the pandemic in Saudi Arabia. Providing vaccination without direct cost to recipients and communicating safety and efficacy evidence transparently may support public confidence and vaccine acceptance during future large-scale immunization campaigns. These findings should be interpreted as an early-pandemic baseline and should not be extrapolated to current post-rollout attitudes.

abstract_zh: 背景:新发传染病爆发期间公众对疫苗的接受程度受到对安全性、可及性和成本的看法的影响。在大流行的早期阶段了解这些决定因素对于制定疫苗接种政策和沟通策略非常重要。本研究探讨了在全国疫苗推出之前,疫苗成本和安全性认知在沙特阿拉伯成年人中塑造 COVID-19 疫苗接种意愿方面的作用。方法:对 2020 年 8 月至 9 月期间居住在沙特阿拉伯的成年人进行了一项横断面电子调查。参与者是通过社交媒体和电子通信渠道在线分发招募的。该调查问卷评估了有关 COVID-19 的社会人口特征、知识和看法,以及在反映疫苗成本以及科学安全性和有效性证据的可用性的五种假设情景下接受 COVID-19 疫苗接种的意愿。进行多变量逻辑回归分析以确定与疫苗接种意愿相关的因素。结果:共有 1293 名受访者完成了调查。当免费提供疫苗接种时,57.5% 的参与者表示他们可能会接种疫苗。随着假设疫苗价格的上涨,疫苗接种意愿下降,当成本超过 100 SAR 时,疫苗接种意愿下降至 38.7%。当在安全性和有效性证据尚未得到证实的情况下接种疫苗时,意愿最低。在多种情况下,年龄、性别、教育程度和之前接种季节性流感疫苗与 COVID-19 疫苗接种意愿相关。结论:在沙特阿拉伯大流行的早期阶段,疫苗的可负担性以及对科学安全性和有效性证据的信心是与 COVID-19 疫苗接种意愿相关的重要因素。在不向接受者产生直接费用的情况下提供疫苗接种,并透明地传达安全性和有效性证据,可能会在未来大规模免疫运动中支持公众信心和疫苗接受度。这些发现应被解释为大流行早期的基线,不应推断为当前推出后的态度。

title: Dynamic-Parameter SIRD Forecasting: ReproducibleTime-Varying Rate Estimation for COVID-19
abstract: Abstract Classical compartmental epidemic models typically assume constant transmission, recovery, and mortality rates, limiting their ability to track policy shifts, behavioral adaptation,and multi-wave outbreaks. We present a hybrid SIRD framework that recovers time-varyingtransition parameters (α(t), β(t), γ(t)) by direct algebraic inversion of surveillance series,models their joint evolution with Vector Autoregression, and integrates the mechanistic system forward. In a 12-step held-out benchmark on a single global COVID-19 aggregate series(2020–2026), evaluated on daily incident counts, the open-source dynasir implementationachieved 39.3% MAPE for new cases and 29.7% for new deaths, outperforming naive persistence (100% for both), static SIRD (116.0% and 172.2%), and ARIMA incidence (631.7%and 79.6%). These correspond to 60.7% and 62.7% reductions relative to the strongest nondynamic reference for each outcome. The estimator maintains O(N) complexity and preserves interpretable R0(t) trajectories. However, nominal 95% prediction intervals achievedonly 33.3% coverage for cases and 41.7% for deaths. The framework is therefore best interpreted as a reproducible point-forecasting baseline for this benchmark pending improvedprobabilistic calibration and broader multi-region or cross-pathogen validation.

abstract_zh: 摘要 经典的区室流行病模型通常假设传播、恢复和死亡率恒定,限制了它们跟踪政策转变、行为适应和多波疫情的能力。我们提出了一种混合 SIRD 框架,该框架通过监视序列的直接代数反演来恢复时变转移参数(α(t),β(t),γ(t)),用向量自回归对其联合演化进行建模,并向前集成机械系统。在针对单个全球 COVID-19 聚合系列(2020-2026)的 12 步坚持基准中,根据每日事件计数进行评估,开源 dynasir 实现的新病例 MAPE 为 39.3%,新死亡病例为 29.7%,优于幼稚持久性(两者均为 100%)、静态 SIRD(116.0% 和 172.2%)以及 ARIMA 发生率(631.7%和79.6%)。相对于每个结果的最强非动态参考,这对应于 60.7% 和 62.7% 的减少。估计器保持 O(N) 复杂度并保留可解释的 R0(t) 轨迹。然而,名义上的 95% 预测区间仅实现了 33.3% 的病例覆盖率和 41.7% 的死亡覆盖率。因此,该框架最好被解释为该基准的可重复点预测基线,等待改进的概率校准和更广泛的多区域或跨病原体验证。

title: Proteomic analysis identifies pathways related to immune dysregulation in patients with hematologic malignancies after COVID-19 infection
abstract: ABSTRACT Patients with hematologic malignancies (HMs) are particularly vulnerable to coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) because of underlying immune dysfunction and treatment-related immunosuppression. However, proteomic features associated with different clinical trajectories in this population remain insufficiently characterized. We performed serum proteomic analysis in 40 HM patients with COVID-19 and 15 healthy controls. Compared with controls, HM patients showed impaired immune-related responses during the acute phase of COVID-19. Acute-phase proteomic patterns differed across outcome groups; however, because outcome groups were closely intertwined with initial COVID-19 severity, ICU admission, and systemic illness, and because multivariable adjustment was not performed due to the limited sample size, these patterns should be interpreted as severity- and outcome-associated profiles rather than independent trajectory-specific markers. Fatal cases showed evidence of dysregulated immune activation, whereas patients later classified as having long COVID exhibited broader suppression of immune-related pathways. In addition to immune alterations, pathways related to platelet activation and cardiac-related dysfunction were associated with adverse clinical trajectories. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay validation supported the association of selected proteins with outcome groups during acute infection. These findings provide a proteomic overview of COVID-19 in HM patients and offer a basis for future mechanistic studies and larger external validation cohorts. IMPORTANCE Patients with hematologic malignancies are highly vulnerable to severe coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), acute death, and long COVID due to preexisting immune dysfunction. However, the proteomic signatures linked to adverse clinical trajectories remain poorly understood. Our serum proteomic study identifies distinct acute-phase immune profiles associated with different outcomes: broad immune suppression characterizes long COVID, while dysregulated immune activation is associated with fatal cases. Platelet activation and cardiac-related pathways are also linked to poor outcomes. These findings provide key molecular insights for this high-risk population, supporting future biomarker development, risk stratification, and targeted clinical management. abstract_zh: 摘要 由于潜在的免疫功能障碍和治疗相关的免疫抑制,血液恶性肿瘤 (HMs) 患者特别容易感染 2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19)。然而,与该人群不同临床轨迹相关的蛋白质组学特征仍未得到充分表征。我们对 40 名患有 COVID-19 的 HM 患者和 15 名健康对照者进行了血清蛋白质组分析。与对照组相比,HM 患者在 COVID-19 急性期表现出免疫相关反应受损。不同结果组的急性期蛋白质组模式有所不同;然而,由于结果组与最初的COVID-19严重程度、ICU入院和全身性疾病密切相关,并且由于样本量有限而未进行多变量调整,因此这些模式应被解释为与严重程度和结果相关的概况,而不是独立的轨迹特异性标记。致命病例显示出免疫激活失调的证据,而后来被分类为长期感染新冠病毒的患者则表现出更广泛的免疫相关途径抑制。除了免疫改变之外,与血小板活化和心脏相关功能障碍相关的途径也与不良临床轨迹相关。酶联免疫吸附测定验证支持所选蛋白质与急性感染期间结果组的关联。这些发现提供了 HM 患者中 COVID-19 的蛋白质组学概述,并为未来的机制研究和更大规模的外部验证队列提供了基础。重要性 由于先前存在的免疫功能障碍,血液系统恶性肿瘤患者极易感染严重的 2019 冠状病毒病 (COVID-19)、急性死亡和长期感染新冠病毒。然而,与不良临床轨迹相关的蛋白质组学特征仍然知之甚少。我们的血清蛋白质组学研究确定了与不同结果相关的不同急性期免疫特征:广泛的免疫抑制是长期新冠肺炎的特征,而免疫激活失调则与致命病例相关。血小板活化和心脏相关通路也与不良结果有关。这些发现为这一高危人群提供了关键的分子见解,支持未来生物标志物的开发、风险分层和有针对性的临床管理。临床试验 本研究在 ClinicalTrials.gov 注册为 NCT05683353。该研究在 ClinicalTrials.gov 注册为 NCT05683353。

title: Association of oral outpatient antiviral medications for COVID-19 with the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 at 28 and 90 days in a cohort of individuals with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases
abstract: Introduction/objectives Prior studies have evaluated the relationship between antiviral medications for COVID-19 and the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC, i.e., "long COVID") in the general population. We evaluated PASC in individuals with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs) by antiviral use, hypothesizing that antivirals are associated with lower PASC risk. Methods We investigated oral outpatient antiviral use (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or molnupiravir) and PASC in a prospective SARD cohort at Mass General Brigham ≥ 28 days following COVID-19 infection (16/December/2021-30/January/2025). Participants completed surveys regarding symptom duration. We investigated odds of PASC at 28 and 90 days following COVID-19 using multivariable logistic regression. Results Among 431 participants (mean age 56.2 years, 81% female), 51% were treated with oral antivirals. The most common SARD type was inflammatory arthritis (46%), 46% were using conventional synthetic DMARDs, and 41% were using biologic DMARDs. Nearly all (96%) were vaccinated at the time of COVID-19 infection. Those who received antivirals had similar odds of PASC at 28 days (30.9% vs. 31.1%, aOR 0.98, 95% CI: 0.64-1.49) and numerically lower odds at 90 days (5.2% vs. 10.5%, aOR 0.44, 95% CI: 0.19-1.02) compared to those who did not receive antivirals. Conclusion In this contemporary cohort, risk of PASC 90 days after COVID-19 onset was overall low. Those who received antiviral therapy had similar odds of PASC at 28 days and numerically lower odds of PASC at 90 days compared to those who did not receive antivirals, providing evidence to quantify PASC risk when considering oral outpatient antiviral treatment. Key Points • Among people with rheumatic diseases, post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) status at 28 days after symptom onset was similar regardless of antiviral use. • Odds of PASC at 90 days were numerically lower with antiviral use. • Patient-reported outcomes were similar regardless of antiviral use.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the association between oral outpatient antiviral medications (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or molnupiravir) and the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in individuals with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs), focusing on outcomes at 28 and 90 days post-infection. The central question is whether antiviral use is associated with a lower risk of PASC in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a prospective cohort study conducted at Mass General Brigham from December 16, 2021, to January 30, 2025. Participants completed surveys regarding symptom duration, and the study used multivariable logistic regression to investigate the odds of PASC at 28 and 90 days following COVID-19 infection. The study included 431 participants, with 51% treated with oral antivirals.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that in this cohort, the risk of PASC 90 days after COVID-19 onset was overall low. Those who received antiviral therapy had similar odds of PASC at 28 days and numerically lower odds of PASC at 90 days compared to those who did not receive antivirals. This provides evidence to quantify PASC risk when considering oral outpatient antiviral treatment. [A12][A13][A14][A15][A16].
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report specific controversies or evidence gaps, but it notes that the risk of PASC at 28 days was similar regardless of antiviral use, while the risk at 90 days was numerically lower with antiviral use. The study did not find significant differences in patient-reported outcomes based on antiviral use. [A9][A10][A11][A16].
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that further research is needed to confirm the numerical reduction in PASC risk at 90 days with antiviral use and to explore the long-term effects of antiviral treatment on PASC in individuals with SARDs. Clinicians may consider these findings when evaluating the potential benefits of antiviral treatment for COVID-19 in this population.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the association between oral outpatient antiviral medications and the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in individuals with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs). The study, conducted at Mass General Brigham from December 16, 2021, to January 30, 2025, included 431 participants, with 51% treated with antivirals. The review found that those who received antiviral therapy had similar odds of PASC at 28 days and numerically lower odds at 90 days compared to those who did not receive antivirals. The overall risk of PASC 90 days after COVID-19 onset was low. The review suggests that further research is needed to confirm these findings and explore long-term effects, while clinicians may consider these results when evaluating antiviral treatment benefits for COVID-19 in individuals with SARDs.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines the association between oral outpatient antiviral medications (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or molnupiravir) and the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) in individuals with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs), focusing on outcomes at 28 and 90 days post-infection. The central question is whether antiviral use is associated with a lower risk of PASC in this population.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a prospective cohort study conducted at Mass General Brigham from December 16, 2021, to January 30, 2025. Participants completed surveys regarding symptom duration, and the study used multivariable logistic regression to investigate the odds of PASC at 28 and 90 days following COVID-19 infection. The study included 431 participants, with 51% treated with oral antivirals.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that in this cohort, the risk of PASC 90 days after COVID-19 onset was overall low. Those who received antiviral therapy had similar odds of PASC at 28 days and numerically lower odds of PASC at 90 days compared to those who did not receive antivirals. This provides evidence to quantify PASC risk when considering oral outpatient antiviral treatment. [A12][A13][A14][A15][A16].
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report specific controversies or evidence gaps, but it notes that the risk of PASC at 28 days was similar regardless of antiviral use, while the risk at 90 days was numerically lower with antiviral use. The study did not find significant differences in patient-reported outcomes based on antiviral use. [A9][A10][A11][A16].
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that further research is needed to confirm the numerical reduction in PASC risk at 90 days with antiviral use and to explore the long-term effects of antiviral treatment on PASC in individuals with SARDs. Clinicians may consider these findings when evaluating the potential benefits of antiviral treatment for COVID-19 in this population.

title_zh: 在一组患有系统性自身免疫性风湿性疾病的患者中,门诊口服抗病毒药物与 COVID-19 28 和 90 天后遗症风险的关系
source_body_en: Introduction/objectives Prior studies have evaluated the relationship between antiviral medications for COVID-19 and the risk of post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC, i.e., "long COVID") in the general population. We evaluated PASC in individuals with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs) by antiviral use, hypothesizing that antivirals are associated with lower PASC risk. Methods We investigated oral outpatient antiviral use (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir or molnupiravir) and PASC in a prospective SARD cohort at Mass General Brigham ≥ 28 days following COVID-19 infection (16/December/2021-30/January/2025). Participants completed surveys regarding symptom duration. We investigated odds of PASC at 28 and 90 days following COVID-19 using multivariable logistic regression. Results Among 431 participants (mean age 56.2 years, 81% female), 51% were treated with oral antivirals. The most common SARD type was inflammatory arthritis (46%), 46% were using conventional synthetic DMARDs, and 41% were using biologic DMARDs. Nearly all (96%) were vaccinated at the time of COVID-19 infection. Those who received antivirals had similar odds of PASC at 28 days (30.9% vs. 31.1%, aOR 0.98, 95% CI: 0.64-1.49) and numerically lower odds at 90 days (5.2% vs. 10.5%, aOR 0.44, 95% CI: 0.19-1.02) compared to those who did not receive antivirals. Conclusion In this contemporary cohort, risk of PASC 90 days after COVID-19 onset was overall low. Those who received antiviral therapy had similar odds of PASC at 28 days and numerically lower odds of PASC at 90 days compared to those who did not receive antivirals, providing evidence to quantify PASC risk when considering oral outpatient antiviral treatment. Key Points • Among people with rheumatic diseases, post-acute sequelae of COVID-19 (PASC) status at 28 days after symptom onset was similar regardless of antiviral use. • Odds of PASC at 90 days were numerically lower with antiviral use. • Patient-reported outcomes were similar regardless of antiviral use.

title: Impact of SARS-CoV-2 variants and demographic factors on COVID-19 severity in pediatric patients
abstract: BACKGROUND: Factors that influence pediatric COVID-19 severity remain incompletely understood, particularly related to the impact of viral and host factors. Understanding the factors contributing to the severity of presentation can impact clinical approaches and management. This study examined the associations between SARS-CoV-2 variants, demographic factors, and COVID-19 severity in a large diverse pediatric population. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study at a large freestanding Children's Hospital (Children's Hospital Los Angeles) from March 2020 through April 2024 including 14,292 patients aged 0-25 years who tested positive for SARS-CoV-2. Viral variants were determined by whole genome sequencing in 6,939 patients (48.6%). COVID-19 severity was classified as mild, moderate, or severe based on hospitalization requirements and need for respiratory support following the World Health Organization Criteria. Disease severity comparisons were made between different viral variants and demographic factors using multinomial logistic regression. RESULTS: Among 14,292 patients, 53.8% were male with median age 5.2 years. Racial/ethnic distribution was 63.0% Hispanic/Latino, 21.4% White, 9.3% African American, and 6.3% Asian. Compared with pre-Omicron variants, Omicron was associated with increased odds of moderate (odds ratio [OR], 2.85; 95% CI, 2.31-3.52; P < 0.001) and severe disease (OR, 3.95; 95% CI, 3.01-5.18; P < 0.001). White patients had lower odds of moderate (OR, 0.81; 95% CI, 0.67-0.98) and severe disease (OR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.64-1.05) compared with non-White patients. Age-race interactions were significant, with different severity patterns across racial groups as age increased. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that both viral variants and host demographic factors contribute meaningfully to pediatric COVID-19 severity. Understanding these interactions would support a more tailored approach to pediatric COVID-19 that considers the impact of viral variants and host demographic factors.

title: Menstrual Cycle Changes among Reproduction-Aged Iranian Women Following COVID-19 Vaccination
abstract: Background: Menstrual cycle disturbances have been increasingly reported after COVID-19 vaccination, raising questions about their prevalence and clinical significance among women of reproductive age. Objective This study aimed to investigate the incidence and types of menstrual cycle alterations following different doses of COVID-19 vaccines among Iranian women of reproductive age. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among vaccinated women who reported their menstrual cycle status before and after each vaccine dose. Data on cycle regularity, flow characteristics, and specific menstrual disorders were collected and analyzed. Results Menstrual cycle alterations were reported by 28.8%, 25.4%, 30.3%, and 68.4% of participants after the first, second, third, and fourth vaccine doses, respectively. The most common changes were oligomenorrhea after the first and second doses (8.9% and 5.6%), menorrhagia after the third dose (5.3%), and hypomenorrhea after the fourth dose (8.3%). Comparisons with international studies revealed a wide variation in prevalence (ranging from 25% to 78%), which may be explained by differences in methodology, population characteristics, vaccine types, and pre-vaccination health status. Conclusion A considerable proportion of Iranian women experienced menstrual alterations following COVID-19 vaccination, most commonly oligomenorrhea, menorrhagia, and hypomenorrhea. While generally self-limiting, these findings highlight the need to integrate menstrual health into post-vaccination monitoring and patient counseling. Future research should explore the underlying immune–endocrine mechanisms and long-term clinical implications of these changes.

abstract_zh: 背景:接种 COVID-19 疫苗后越来越多地报道月经周期紊乱,这引发了人们对其在育龄妇女中的患病率和临床意义的疑问。目的 本研究旨在调查伊朗育龄妇女接种不同剂量的 COVID-19 疫苗后月经周期改变的发生率和类型。方法 对已接种疫苗的女性进行横断面调查,报告每次疫苗接种前后的月经周期状况。收集并分析有关周期规律、血流特征和特定月经失调的数据。结果 在接种第一剂、第二剂、第三剂和第四剂疫苗后,分别有 28.8%、25.4%、30.3% 和 68.4% 的参与者报告月经周期发生变化。最常见的变化是第一剂和第二剂后月经稀发(8.9%和5.6%)、第三剂后月经过多(5.3%)和第四剂后月经量少(8.3%)。与国际研究的比较显示,患病率存在​​很大差异(从 25% 到 78%),这可能是由于方法、人群特征、疫苗类型和接种前健康状况的差异所致。结论 相当比例的伊朗女性在接种 COVID-19 疫苗后出现月经改变,最常见的是月经稀发、月经过多和月经量少。虽然这些发现通常具有自我限制性,但强调需要将月经健康纳入疫苗接种后监测和患者咨询中。未来的研究应该探索潜在的免疫内分泌机制以及这些变化的长期临床影响。

title: Understanding Mental Health in Crisis: Key Determinants of Psychological Distress in Belgium during the first weeks of COVID-19 Lockdown
abstract: Aims: : The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly impacted global mental health. At the onset of the pandemic (2020), Belgians experienced increased anxiety, depression, and psychological distress compared to 2018 due to the outbreak and the associated public health measures. Understanding the drivers of this distress is crucial for mitigating mental health effects in future crises. This study examines determinants of psychological distress in Belgium during the March 2020 lockdown, using data from the Great Corona Study (GCS). Methods: Data were drawn from the second wave of the GCS, a citizen science initiative conducted in Belgium on March 24, 2020, with 332,169 respondents. Psychological distress was measured using the General Health Questionnaire-12 (GHQ-12), applying a 2/3 cutoff to classify distress levels. To identify predictor variables, a random forest algorithm and literature review reduced 207 initial variables to 16. A generalized linear model was then used to examine associations between predictors and psychological distress Results: Psychological distress was significantly associated with various demographic, social, occupational, and health-related factors. Younger individuals, women, and residents of Wallonia or Brussels exhibited higher odds of distress. Household composition, and the frequency of real-life social interactions significantly influenced distress levels. Occupational status played a key role, with part-time employees and working students exhibiting higher levels of distress. At the same time retired individuals with no current occupation showed lower odds. Perceived workplace safety and compliance with public health measures also significantly impacted distress levels. Lastly, individuals experiencing influenza-like or COVID-19 symptoms had substantially higher odds of psychological distress. Conclusions: Our findings highlight significant sociodemographic, occupational, and health-related predictors of psychological distress during the initial COVID-19 lockdown in Belgium. Young adults, women, individuals with limited in-person interactions, and those experiencing influenza-like illness or COVID-19 symptoms were particularly vulnerable. Additionally, perceptions of others' adherence to preventive measures played a crucial role in mental well-being. These results highlight the complex interplay between individual and environmental factors in shaping psychological distress, providing valuable insights for future public health policies and mental health interventions during crises.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The COVID-19 pandemic caused a measurable rise in psychological distress in Belgium during early 2020, yet the specific determinants of this distress remained insufficiently understood. The study aimed to identify key drivers of psychological distress during the March 2020 lockdown to inform future crisis mental-health responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional analysis was conducted using data from the Great Corona Study (GCS), a citizen science initiative in Belgium. The study surveyed 332,169 respondents on March 24, 2020, during the first COVID-19 lockdown.
analysis.methods: Psychological distress was assessed with the General Health Questionnaire-12 (GHQ-12) using a 2/3 cutoff. A random forest algorithm and literature review reduced 207 candidate variables to 16 predictors, which were then analyzed using a generalized linear model to examine associations with distress.
analysis.main_results: Psychological distress was significantly associated with younger age, female sex, residence in Wallonia or Brussels, household composition, frequency of real-life social interactions, occupational status (higher odds in part-time employees and working students, lower odds in retired individuals), perceived workplace safety, compliance with public health measures, and the presence of influenza-like or COVID-19 symptoms.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that sociodemographic, occupational, and health-related factors jointly shaped psychological distress during the lockdown. The novelty lies in quantifying the relative importance of these determinants in a large, real-time citizen science dataset.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results can inform targeted mental health interventions and public health policies by identifying high-risk groups (e.g., young adults, women, part-time workers) and modifiable factors (e.g., social interaction frequency, workplace safety perceptions) during future crises.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and reliance on self-reported symptoms and behaviors may introduce bias. Despite the large sample size, the generalizability to other contexts or later pandemic phases is uncertain, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed determinants of psychological distress among 332,169 Belgians during the March 2020 COVID-19 lockdown using data from the Great Corona Study. Psychological distress was measured with the GHQ-12, and 16 predictors were identified through a random forest algorithm and literature review before being analyzed with a generalized linear model. Higher odds of distress were observed among younger individuals, women, residents of Wallonia or Brussels, part-time employees, working students, and those with limited in-person interactions or influenza-like symptoms. Lower odds were seen in retired individuals. Perceived workplace safety and compliance with public health measures also significantly impacted distress levels. The authors highlight the complex interplay between sociodemographic, occupational, and health-related factors, offering insights for crisis mental health interventions.

abstract_zh: 目标::COVID-19 大流行严重影响了全球心理健康。在大流行爆发时(2020 年),由于疫情爆发和相关的公共卫生措施,与 2018 年相比,比利时人的焦虑、抑郁和心理困扰有所增加。了解这种痛苦的驱动因素对于减轻未来危机中的心理健康影响至关重要。本研究利用大新冠研究 (GCS) 的数据,探讨了 2020 年 3 月封锁期间比利时心理困扰的决定因素。方法:数据来自第二波 GCS,这是一项于 2020 年 3 月 24 日在比利时开展的公民科学倡议,共有 332,169 名受访者。使用一般健康问卷 12 (GHQ-12) 测量心理困扰,并应用 2/3 截止值对困扰级别进行分类。为了确定预测变量,随机森林算法和文献综述将 207 个初始变量减少到 16 个。然后使用广义线性模型来检查预测变量和心理困扰之间的关联。结果:心理困扰与各种人口、社会、职业和健康相关因素显着相关。瓦隆或布鲁塞尔的年轻人、女性和居民表现出更高的痛苦几率。家庭组成和现实生活中社交互动的频率显着影响痛苦程度。职业地位发挥了关键作用,兼职员工和在职学生表现出更高程度的痛苦。与此同时,目前没有职业的退休人员的赔率较低。对工作场所安全的感知和对公共卫生措施的遵守也显着影响了痛苦程度。最后,出现流感样症状或 COVID-19 症状的人出现心理困扰的几率要高得多。结论:我们的研究结果强调了比利时 COVID-19 最初封锁期间心理困扰的重要社会人口、职业和健康相关预测因素。年轻人、女性、面对面互动有限的个人以及患有流感样疾病或 COVID-19 症状的人尤其容易受到影响。此外,对其他人遵守预防措施的看法对心理健康也起着至关重要的作用。这些结果凸显了个人和环境因素在形成心理困扰方面的复杂相互作用,为未来的公共卫生政策和危机期间的心理健康干预措施提供了宝贵的见解。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 2020 年初,Covid-19 大流行导致比利时心理困扰明显增加,但造成这种困扰的具体决定因素仍不清楚。该研究旨在确定 2020 年 3 月封锁期间心理困扰的关键驱动因素,为未来的危机心理健康应对措施提供信息。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用来自比利时公民科学倡议“大新冠研究”(GCS) 的数据进行了横断面分析。该研究于 2020 年 3 月 24 日(即首次 COVID-19 封锁期间)对 332,169 名受访者进行了调查。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用一般健康问卷 12 (GHQ-12) 使用 2/3 截止点评估心理困扰。随机森林算法和文献综述将 207 个候选变量减少为 16 个预测变量,然后使用广义线性模型对其进行分析,以检查与痛苦的关联。
analysis_zh.main_results: 心理困扰与年龄较小、女性、居住在瓦隆或布鲁塞尔、家庭构成、现实生活中社交互动的频率、职业状态(兼职员工和在职学生的几率较高,退休人员的几率较低)、工作场所安全感知、公共卫生措施的遵守情况以及流感样或 COVID-19 症状的存在显着相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为社会人口、职业和健康相关因素共同影响封锁期间心理困扰的证据。新颖之处在于量化大型实时公民科学数据集中这些决定因素的相对重要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以通过识别未来危机期间的高风险群体(例如年轻人、妇女、兼职工人)和可改变因素(例如社交互动频率、工作场所安全观念)来为有针对性的心理健康干预措施和公共卫生政策提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 横断面设计排除了因果推断,并且依赖自我报告的症状和行为可能会引入偏见。尽管样本量很大,但对其他情况或大流行后期阶段的普遍性尚不确定,需要谨慎解释。

title: Systematic review of amino acid profiles among COVID-19 patients caused by SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Abstract Background Emerging evidence highlights the critical role of amino acid metabolism in the pathogenesis and severity of COVID-19. This review included studies encompassing patients with varying degrees of disease severity, from mild to critical cases. Methods A systematic review following PRISMA guidelines was conducted, and study quality was appraised using the Newcastle–Ottawa tools to explore the relationship between amino acid profiles and clinical outcomes in COVID-19 patients. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (from the start of the pandemic through the most recent data available on December 2024) identified peer-reviewed studies reporting original data on amino acid metabolism in COVID-19 patients. Results Fourteen eligiblestudies involving 1355 confirmed COVID-19 patients (1726 total participants) were included and revealed significant disruptions inamino acid profiles. Key findings included reduced levels of arginine, glutamine, and tryptophan, alongside elevated phenylalanine andbranched-chain amino acids (BCAAs). These changes were associated with disease severity, immune suppression, systemicinflammation, and metabolic reprogramming. Dysregulation of pathways such as the urea cycle and kynurenine pathway were linked toendothelial dysfunction and immune dysregulation. Conclusions Dysregulated amino acid profiles may serve as potential biomarkers for disease severity and require further validation before clinical application. Restoring amino acid balance or modulating metabolic pathways could improve clinical outcomes. Further research is needed to validate these findings and explore personalized treatment strategies aimed at mitigating the metabolic consequences of SARS-CoV-2 infection.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) in human hosts, focusing on amino acid metabolism as a determinant of disease severity and clinical outcomes, with a central question on how amino acid profile disruptions relate to pathogenesis and severity.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review following PRISMA guidelines searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar from the start of the pandemic through December 2024, including peer-reviewed studies reporting original data on amino acid metabolism in COVID-19 patients, with study quality appraised using the Newcastle–Ottawa tools.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Fourteen studies involving 1355 confirmed COVID-19 patients (1726 total participants) reported significant disruptions in amino acid profiles, including reduced arginine, glutamine, and tryptophan, alongside elevated phenylalanine and branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), associated with disease severity, immune suppression, systemic inflammation, and metabolic reprogramming.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights heterogeneity in study designs and populations, with no pooled estimates reported, and notes that dysregulated pathways such as the urea cycle and kynurenine pathway are linked to endothelial dysfunction and immune dysregulation but remain insufficiently characterized in diverse clinical contexts.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Validation of amino acid profiles as biomarkers for disease severity and exploration of personalized treatment strategies targeting metabolic pathways are needed to improve clinical outcomes in COVID-19 patients.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review investigates the role of amino acid metabolism in COVID-19 pathogenesis and severity among human patients. Using PRISMA-guided searches across major databases up to December 2024, it synthesized evidence from 14 studies involving 1355 confirmed cases, identifying consistent disruptions in amino acid profiles—reductions in arginine, glutamine, and tryptophan, and elevations in phenylalanine and BCAAs—linked to disease severity, immune suppression, and systemic inflammation. Dysregulation of metabolic pathways such as the urea cycle and kynurenine pathway was associated with endothelial and immune dysfunction. The review concludes that these metabolic disturbances may serve as biomarkers for severity but require further validation before clinical application. Key gaps include heterogeneity in study designs and insufficient characterization of pathway-specific mechanisms across diverse populations.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了人类宿主中的 SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19),重点关注氨基酸代谢作为疾病严重程度和临床结果的决定因素,核心问题是氨基酸谱破坏如何与发病机制和严重程度相关。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 一项遵循 PRISMA 指南的系统综述检索了从大流行开始到 2024 年 12 月的 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science 和 Google Scholar,其中包括报告 COVID-19 患者氨基酸代谢原始数据的同行评审研究,并使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华工具评估了研究质量。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 涉及 1355 名确诊的 COVID-19 患者(总共 1726 名参与者)的 14 项研究报告了氨基酸谱的显着破坏,包括精氨酸、谷氨酰胺和色氨酸的减少,以及苯丙氨酸和支链氨基酸 (BCAA) 的升高,这些与疾病严重程度、免疫抑制、全身炎症和代谢重编程相关。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了研究设计和人群的异质性,没有报告汇总估计值,并指出尿素循环和犬尿氨酸途径等失调途径与内皮功能障碍和免疫失调有关,但在不同的临床背景下仍然没有充分表征。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 为了改善 COVID-19 患者的临床结果,需要验证氨基酸谱作为疾病严重程度的生物标志物,并探索针对代谢途径的个性化治疗策略。

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 新出现的证据强调了氨基酸代谢在 COVID-19 发病机制和严重程度中的关键作用。该综述纳入的研究涵盖了疾病严重程度从轻度到危重的不同程度的患者。方法 按照 PRISMA 指南进行系统评价,并使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华工具评估研究质量,以探讨氨基酸谱与 COVID-19 患者临床结果之间的关系。对 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science 和 Google Scholar 的全面搜索(从大流行开始到 2024 年 12 月的最新数据)发现了报告 COVID-19 患者氨基酸代谢原始数据的同行评审研究。结果 纳入了 14 项符合条件的研究,涉及 1355 名确诊的 COVID-19 患者(总共 1726 名参与者),结果显示氨基酸谱存在显着破坏。主要发现包括精氨酸、谷氨酰胺和色氨酸水平降低,同时苯丙氨酸和支链氨基酸 (BCAA) 水平升高。这些变化与疾病严重程度、免疫抑制、全身炎症和代谢重编程有关。尿素循环和犬尿氨酸途径等途径的失调与内皮功能障碍和免疫失调有关。结论 失调的氨基酸谱可能作为疾病严重程度的潜在生物标志物,在临床应用前需要进一步验证。恢复氨基酸平衡或调节代谢途径可以改善临床结果。需要进一步的研究来验证这些发现,并探索旨在减轻 SARS-CoV-2 感染的代谢后果的个性化治疗策略。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了人类宿主中的 SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19),重点关注氨基酸代谢作为疾病严重程度和临床结果的决定因素,核心问题是氨基酸谱破坏如何与发病机制和严重程度相关。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 一项遵循 PRISMA 指南的系统综述检索了从大流行开始到 2024 年 12 月的 PubMed、Scopus、Web of Science 和 Google Scholar,其中包括报告 COVID-19 患者氨基酸代谢原始数据的同行评审研究,并使用纽卡斯尔-渥太华工具评估了研究质量。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 涉及 1355 名确诊的 COVID-19 患者(总共 1726 名参与者)的 14 项研究报告了氨基酸谱的显着破坏,包括精氨酸、谷氨酰胺和色氨酸的减少,以及苯丙氨酸和支链氨基酸 (BCAA) 的升高,这些与疾病严重程度、免疫抑制、全身炎症和代谢重编程相关。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了研究设计和人群的异质性,没有报告汇总估计值,并指出尿素循环和犬尿氨酸途径等失调途径与内皮功能障碍和免疫失调有关,但在不同的临床背景下仍然没有充分表征。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 为了改善 COVID-19 患者的临床结果,需要验证氨基酸谱作为疾病严重程度的生物标志物,并探索针对代谢途径的个性化治疗策略。

title: Neutralisation capacity against SARS-CoV-2 ancestral, Delta and Omicron variants before and after heterologous booster vaccination in Fijian health system workers
abstract: Abstract Immunogenicity studies of booster doses of COVID-19 vaccines from Pacific Island countries are limited. A prospective cohort study was conducted amongst healthcare workers in Fiji to assess antibody neutralisation capacity against ancestral, Delta and Omicron (BA.2) variants following high force of infection from Delta during administration of primary dose schedules. Findings showed high baseline neutralisation prior to heterologous booster vaccinations and enduring protective neutralisation against all three variants of SARS-CoV2 at 6 months following booster receipt. Limited benefit from third doses in this population emphasises the need for pragmatic vaccination strategies guided by local disease contexts.

title: COVID-19 status and intensive care unit burden and mortality: a single-center retrospective cohort study comparing COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 admissions
abstract: BACKGROUND: Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) placed substantial pressure on intensive care units (ICUs), but long-period comparisons with non-COVID-19 ICU patients remain useful for distinguishing disease-associated patterns from the general burden of critical illness. We addressed the gap in single-center data linking COVID-19 status with mortality, healthcare-associated infections, admission physiology, and Therapeutic Intervention Scoring System-28 (TISS-28) workload in a mixed tertiary ICU. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included first admissions to the adult ICU of the University Clinical Hospital in Białystok, Poland, between January 1, 2017, and June 1, 2023. Patients were classified as COVID-19-positive (n = 355) or COVID-19-negative (n = 2971) according to reverse transcription-polymerase chain reaction testing. Baseline characteristics, comorbidities, healthcare-associated infections, admission laboratory and arterial blood gas variables, and TISS-28 variables were compared using Welch t-tests, chi-square tests, or Fisher exact tests, as appropriate. Effect sizes are reported with 95% confidence intervals. Logistic regression estimated the association between COVID-19 status and in-hospital mortality in unadjusted, baseline-adjusted, and exploratory complete-case models. RESULTS: In-hospital mortality was higher in COVID-19-positive patients than in COVID-19-negative patients (227/355 [63.9%] vs. 1320/2971 [44.4%]; odds ratio [OR] 2.22, 95% CI 1.77 to 2.79). This association remained after baseline adjustment (adjusted OR 2.03, 95% CI 1.60 to 2.58) and in the exploratory complete-case model including admission physiology and laboratory markers (adjusted OR 2.73, 95% CI 1.60 to 4.64). Among non-survivors, time to death was shorter in the COVID-19-positive group (10.7 [SD 7.4] vs. 14.3 [SD 20.0] days; mean difference - 3.63 days, 95% CI -5.07 to -2.18). Bacterial bloodstream infection was more frequent in COVID-19-positive patients (22.8% vs. 9.9%; OR 2.70, 95% CI 2.05 to 3.56). At admission, COVID-19-positive patients had lower C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, PaO2, creatinine, and lactate, but higher PaCO2, glucose, sodium, potassium, bicarbonate, and hemoglobin values. TISS-28 profiles differed by COVID-19 status, most notably for respiratory physiotherapy recorded at least once (97.5% vs. 62.0%; OR 23.63, 95% CI 11.76 to 47.52) and longer duration of respiratory physiotherapy (mean difference 4.89 days, 95% CI 3.57 to 6.22). CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort, COVID-19-positive status was associated with higher in-hospital mortality, shorter time to death among non-survivors, more frequent bacterial bloodstream infection, and a distinct ICU workload profile. These findings should be interpreted as associations rather than causal effects because of the single-center design, long heterogeneous study period, incomplete severity-score data, and lack of shift-level staffing and high-dependency-unit data.

title: Microvascular Thrombosis and Acute Kidney Injury in COVID-19: A Systematic Review and Quantitative Analysis
abstract: Abstract Objective: To synthesize the available evidence on the association between SARS-CoV-2-related microvascular thrombosis and acute kidney injury (AKI), with emphasis on renal outcomes, mortality, and renal replacement therapy requirements. Methods: This systematic review followed the PRISMA 2020 statement and was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251132701). PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Embase were searched for systematic reviews, including meta-analyses, and umbrella reviews investigating the association between SARS-CoV-2-related microvascular thrombosis and acute kidney injury. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and methodological quality assessment using AMSTAR-2 and ROBIS. Evidence was synthesized through a structured narrative synthesis supported by quantitative data extracted from the included reviews. Results: Six evidence syntheses evaluating kidney involvement, thrombotic events, and microvascular mechanisms in COVID-19 were included. AKI incidence was 9.2% (95%CI 4.6-13.9) among hospitalized patients and 32.6% (95%CI 8.5-56.6) among critically ill patients. In children with multisystem inflammatory syndrome associated with SARS-CoV-2, AKI incidence was 20% (95%CI 14-28). Microvascular or thrombotic events were associated with adverse renal outcomes (OR 2.14; 95%CI 1.32-3.48). AKI was associated with increased mortality (OR 4.68; 95%CI 1.06-20.70) and greater likelihood of renal replacement therapy requirement (OR 2.87; 95%CI 1.45-5.68). The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to high for the principal outcomes. Conclusion: Current evidence supports an important association between microvascular thrombotic injury and COVID-19-associated AKI. These findings reinforce the relevance of endothelial dysfunction and thromboinflammatory pathways in kidney involvement during COVID-19 and highlight the need for early renal monitoring, risk stratification, and kidney-protective strategies in high-risk patients. Keywords: COVID-19; Acute Kidney Injury; Microvascular Thrombosis; SARS-CoV-2; Renal Replacement Therapy; Systematic Review

abstract_zh: 摘要 目的:综合 SARS-CoV-2 相关微血管血栓形成与急性肾损伤 (AKI) 之间关联的现有证据,重点关注肾脏结局、死亡率和肾脏替代治疗需求。方法:本系统评价遵循 PRISMA 2020 声明,并前瞻性地在 PROSPERO 中注册(CRD420251132701)。检索了 PubMed/MEDLINE、Scopus 和 Embase 的系统综述,包括荟萃分析和伞式综述,调查 SARS-CoV-2 相关微血管血栓形成与急性肾损伤之间的关联。两名评审员使用 AMSTAR-2 和 ROBIS 独立进行研究选择、数据提取和方法学质量评估。通过结构化叙述综合来综合证据,并辅以从纳入的评论中提取的定量数据。结果:纳入了评估 COVID-19 肾脏受累、血栓事件和微血管机制的六项证据综合。住院患者中 AKI 发生率为 9.2%(95%CI 4.6-13.9),危重患者中 AKI 发生率为 32.6%(95%CI 8.5-56.6)。在患有与 SARS-CoV-2 相关的多系统炎症综合征的儿童中,AKI 发生率为 20% (95%CI 14-28)。微血管或血栓事件与不良肾脏结局相关(OR 2.14;95%CI 1.32-3.48)。AKI 与死亡率增加(OR 4.68;95%CI 1.06-20.70)以及需要肾脏替代治疗的可能性更大(OR 2.87;95%CI 1.45-5.68)相关。主要结果的证据质量从中到高不等。结论:当前证据支持微血管血栓性损伤与 COVID-19 相关 AKI 之间存在重要关联。这些发现强化了内皮功能障碍和血栓炎症途径与 COVID-19 期间肾脏受累的相关性,并强调了对高危患者进行早期肾脏监测、风险分层和肾脏保护策略的必要性。关键词:COVID-19;急性肾损伤;微血管血栓形成;SARS-CoV-2;肾脏替代治疗;系统审查

title: The indirect oncological burden of the COVID-19 pandemic: global disruptions in lung cancer diagnosis, surgical management, and healthcare system resilience — a narrative review
abstract: Abstract Background The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic imposed substantial challenges on healthcare systems worldwide, significantly influencing the diagnosis, treatment processes, and clinical outcomes of patients with lung cancer. This article aims to evaluate the indirect oncological consequences of the pandemic, with particular emphasis on delays in diagnosis, staging, and surgical treatment from a thoracic surgery perspective. Methods During the pandemic, extensive structural and administrative transformations were implemented in hospitals, including reorganization of clinical services, allocation of dedicated COVID-19 units, postponement of elective procedures, and redistribution of healthcare resources. While these measures were essential for infection control, they significantly limited access to routine oncological care. This study was designed as a narrative review. Literature was searched in PubMed databases for studies published between January 2020 and February 2026 using combinations of the terms “COVID-19”, “lung cancer”, “thoracic surgery”, “delay diagnosis”. English-language articles evaluating the impact of the pandemic on lung cancer diagnosis, staging, treatment, and outcomes were included. Relevant studies were selected based on clinical relevance and methodological quality. Case reports were excluded from the study as exclusion criteria. Results Evidence from multiple international studies demonstrates substantial reductions in lung cancer diagnoses, decreased surgical volumes, prolonged referral and treatment intervals, and a shift toward more advanced disease stages at presentation. Screening interruptions, patient reluctance to seek medical attention, and restricted diagnostic procedures contributed to a global “diagnostic deficit.” Although surgical outcomes remained generally safe when appropriate protective protocols were applied, treatment delays and altered therapeutic strategies, including increased use of radiotherapy and systemic therapies, raised concerns regarding long-term oncological outcomes. Overall, the pandemic highlighted the vulnerability of cancer care systems during global health crises while also demonstrating that continuity of thoracic oncology services can be maintained through structured protocols and dedicated pathways. Conclusion These findings underscore the necessity of developing resilient healthcare systems capable of preserving timely cancer diagnosis and treatment during future pandemics to minimize indirect mortality and loss of life-years among lung cancer patients.

abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 2019 年冠状病毒病(COVID-19)大流行给全球医疗保健系统带来了巨大挑战,显着影响了肺癌患者的诊断、治疗过程和临床结果。本文旨在评估大流行的间接肿瘤学后果,特别强调从胸外科角度诊断、分期和手术治疗的延误。方法 在大流行期间,医院实施了广泛的结构和行政改革,包括重组临床服务、分配专门的 COVID-19 病房、推迟择期手术以及重新分配医疗资源。虽然这些措施对于控制感染至关重要,但它们极大地限制了获得常规肿瘤护理的机会。本研究旨在作为叙述性回顾。在 PubMed 数据库中检索了 2020 年 1 月至 2026 年 2 月期间发表的研究文献,其中使用了术语“COVID-19”、“肺癌”、“胸外科”、“延迟诊断”的组合。其中包括评估大流行对肺癌诊断、分期、治疗和结果影响的英文文章。根据临床相关性和方法学质量选择相关研究。作为排除标准,病例报告被排除在研究之外。结果 来自多项国际研究的证据表明,肺癌诊断数量大幅减少、手术量减少、转诊和治疗间隔延长以及就诊时疾病阶段向更晚期的转变。筛查中断、患者不愿就医以及诊断程序受限导致了全球“诊断缺陷”。尽管在应用适当的保护方案时,手术结果总体上仍然是安全的,但治疗延迟和治疗策略的改变,包括增加放射治疗和全身治疗的使用,引起了人们对长期肿瘤结果的担忧。总体而言,这场大流行凸显了全球健康危机期间癌症护理系统的脆弱性,同时也表明可以通过结构化方案和专用途径维持胸部肿瘤服务的连续性。结论 这些发现强调了开发有弹性的医疗保健系统的必要性,该系统能够在未来的大流行期间保持及时的癌症诊断和治疗,以最大限度地减少肺癌患者的间接死亡率和生命年损失。

title: Genomic and Antigenic Evolution of Influenza A(H3N2) After the COVID-19 Era: A Scoping Review with Focus on J and K Subclades and Implications for Vaccine Effectiveness
abstract: Post-COVID-19, influenza A(H3N2) has re-emerged with accelerated genetic diversification. The rise in antigenically drifted subclades raises concerns regarding immune escape and vaccine mismatch. To synthesize the available evidence on the post-pandemic evolution of influenza A(H3N2), with particular attention to emerging subclades and their potential public health implications, a scoping review (PRISMA-ScR) was conducted across six databases in January 2026, including studies on genomic surveillance, antigenic characterization, and vaccine effectiveness (VE). Twenty studies were included. While clade 2a.3a.1 (J lineage) predominated, reports highlighted the rapid emergence of the antigenically distinct K subclade (formerly J.2.4.1). Genetic and laboratory assays (HI/neutralization) confirmed immune escape and reduced vaccine match. Observational estimates indicated diminished VE against drifted strains, though no consistent increase in clinical severity was observed. Post-pandemic A(H3N2) is defined by rapid drift and diversification. Emerging variants like the K subclade challenge vaccine selection and seasonal preparedness. Integrated surveillance remains vital for timely vaccine updates and mitigating public health impact.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述研究了后 COVID-19 时代甲型流感 (H3N2) 的基因组和抗原进化,重点关注 J 和 K 亚支及其对疫苗有效性的影响。核心问题涉及这些分支中加速的遗传多样性和抗原漂移如何影响免疫逃逸和疫苗错配。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 2026 年 1 月,对六个数据库进行了范围界定审查 (PRISMA-ScR),以综合有关大流行后甲型 H3N2 流感演变的证据,包括基因组监测、抗原特征和疫苗有效性。根据预先确定的资格标准纳入了二十项研究。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 大流行后甲型流感 (H3N2) 的特点是快速遗传多样性和 2a.3a.1 分支(J 谱系)的优势,以及抗原独特的 K 亚分支的快速出现。遗传和实验室检测(HI/中和)证实了免疫逃逸并减少了漂移毒株的疫苗匹配,观察估计表明疫苗针对这些变异的有效性降低。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述强调了各个分支之间抗原漂移和免疫逃逸的异质性,对于疫苗匹配减少是否会导致临床严重程度的持续增加存在相互矛盾的发现。此外,证据基础缺乏抗原表征和疫苗有效性估计的标准化方法,限制了研究之间的可比性。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 像 K 这样的抗原性不同的亚支的出现对季节性疫苗株的选择提出了挑战,并且需要综合基因组和抗原监测来及时更新疫苗。加强监测系统并协调抗原表征和疫苗有效性评估的方法对于减轻公共卫生影响至关重要。

title: Complex intra-host SARS-CoV-2 evolution following monoclonal antibody pre-exposure prophylaxis
abstract: BackgroundMonoclonal antibodies have emerged as a prophylactic strategy to prevent symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection in immunocompromised individuals. However, the evolutionary and clinical implications of breakthrough infections under this regime remain unclear. MethodsA male in their 80s with a haematological/oncological diagnosis received a 2000 mg intravenous infusion of sotrovimab in March 2023 and was diagnosed with COVID-19 by RT-qPCR from a nasopharyngeal swab in August 2023. Weekly samples (n=24) were collected through February 2024 (171 days). All samples underwent whole-genome sequencing, with select mutations subjected to functional assessment. FindingsSequencing identified the GE.1 lineage at all timepoints. An intra-host recombination event in ORF1ab (positions 8942-12458) was detected prior to 23 weeks post-detection, followed by a 14-fold increase in viral load (7.42e+06 to 1.00e+08 RNA copies/mL) and a marked shift in the viral population. E340D, a sotrovimab resistance mutation, was detected at low abundance (46%) within the first week post-infection, fluctuated over time, and was nearly fixed by week 15 (107 days) post-detection. We assessed five spike mutations - V36M, S98F, and V213G in the N-terminal domain, Y505P in the receptor-binding domain, and P681Q near the S1/S2 cleavage site- and additionally evaluated the impact of E340D. V36M conferred the highest infectivity across all cell lines, with the most significant effect in low-TMPRSS2 cells. While all mutations showed enhanced infectivity with the addition of E340D, the effect was most pronounced in mutations with lower baseline infectivity. The addition of E340D significantly decreased relative neutralizing titres for V36M, S98F, and V213G, enabling escape from neutralizing antibodies in XBB-responsive individuals, illustrating an enhanced phenotypic advantage. Patient neutralizing activity was absent pre-sotrovimab, and sotrovimab-induced neutralization was further compromised by selection of E340D. InterpretationSotrovimab pre-exposure prophylaxis in an immunocompromised patient did not prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection, and selected for resistant mutation E340D, with unexpected fitness consequences across non-receptor binding domain spike regions. analysis.research_question_and_background: Monoclonal antibodies like sotrovimab are used prophylactically in immunocompromised individuals to prevent SARS-CoV-2 infection, but the evolutionary and clinical consequences of breakthrough infections under this regimen remain poorly understood.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single immunocompromised male patient in their 80s with a haematological/oncological diagnosis received 2000 mg intravenous sotrovimab in March 2023 and was diagnosed with COVID-19 by RT-qPCR in August 2023.
analysis.methods: Weekly nasopharyngeal swabs (n=24) were collected over 171 days and subjected to whole-genome sequencing, with select spike mutations functionally assessed in cell lines and neutralization assays.
analysis.main_results: An intra-host recombination event in ORF1ab preceded a 14-fold viral load increase (7.42e+06 to 1.00e+08 RNA copies/mL) and a population shift, while the sotrovimab resistance mutation E340D emerged at 46% abundance initially, fluctuated over time, and became nearly fixed by day 107.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Sotrovimab prophylaxis failed to prevent infection and selected for E340D, which, when combined with other spike mutations, enhanced infectivity and reduced neutralization sensitivity, revealing unexpected fitness trade-offs in non-RBD regions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings caution against sotrovimab prophylaxis in immunocompromised patients due to the risk of selecting resistant variants with altered transmissibility and immune escape potential.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-patient, observational design and absence of control groups limit generalizability and causal inference, warranting low confidence in broader applicability.

analysis.summary_en: This study tracked intra-host SARS-CoV-2 evolution in an immunocompromised patient who received sotrovimab prophylaxis and later developed COVID-19. Weekly sampling over 171 days revealed an intra-host recombination event followed by a 14-fold viral load surge and a population shift. The sotrovimab resistance mutation E340D emerged early, fluctuated, and became dominant by day 107. Functional assays showed E340D, when combined with other spike mutations, increased infectivity—particularly in low-TMPRSS2 cells—and reduced neutralization sensitivity, enabling escape from XBB-responsive antibodies. Prophylaxis failed to prevent infection, and the resistant variant exhibited unexpected fitness advantages across non-receptor binding domain regions. The single-patient design and lack of controls constrain generalizability, indicating low confidence in extrapolating these findings.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 像 sotrovimab 这样的单克隆抗体可预防性地用于免疫功能低下的个体,以防止 SARS-CoV-2 感染,但该方案下突破性感染的进化和临床后果仍知之甚少。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一名患有血液学/肿瘤学诊断的 80 多岁免疫功能低下男性患者于 2023 年 3 月接受了 2000 mg 静脉注射 sotrovimab,并于 2023 年 8 月通过 RT-qPCR 诊断为 COVID-19。
analysis_zh.methods: 171 天内每周收集鼻咽拭子 (n=24),并进行全基因组测序,并在细胞系和中和测定中对选择的刺突突变进行功能评估。
analysis_zh.main_results: ORF1ab 中的宿主内重组事件先于病毒载量增加 14 倍(7.42e+06 至 1.00e+08 RNA 拷贝/mL)和群体转变,而 sotrovimab 抗性突变 E340D 最初以 46% 的丰度出现,随时间波动,并在第 107 天几乎固定。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: Sotrovimab 预防未能预防感染,并选择了 E340D,当与其他刺突突变结合时,它增强了感染性并降低了中和敏感性,揭示了非 RBD 区域中意想不到的适应性权衡。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现警告免疫功能低下患者不要使用 sotrovimab 预防,因为存在选择具有改变的传播性和免疫逃逸潜力的耐药变异的风险。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 单患者、观察性设计和对照组的缺乏限制了普遍性和因果推断,导致对更广泛的适用性缺乏信心。

title: Systemic immune profiling of heterologous versus homologous boosting of COVID-19 vaccination
abstract: BACKGROUND: Compared with homologous boosting, heterologous boosting with a different COVID-19 vaccine following priming generates stronger antibody responses against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) as well as variants, particularly for inactivated COVID-19 vaccine(CoronaVac). However, it is still unclear about the potential immune enhancement mechanism underlying heterologous boosting. METHODS: In this study, we isolated spike protein binding-specific monoclonal antibodies at day 180 post a homologous booster with CoronaVac or a heterologous booster with Ad5-nCoV based on two-dose of CoronaVac using the single B cell sorting platform. Subsequently, we verified their neutralization activity to SARS-CoV-2 variants, germline gene sequences and affinity kinetics targeting SARS-CoV-2 NTD/RBD/S1. Additionally, we conducted an in-depth analysis of the immunological response characteristics, by integrating single-cell RNA/V(D)J sequencing(scRNA/ V(D)J-seq). RESULTS: Our study demonstrated that heterologous boosting with Ad5-nCoV elicited more mature B cells with higher affinity and activated more abundant immune-related pathways compared to the homologous boosting with CoronaVac. In addition, Ad5-nCoV boosting expanded unique clonal types of B and T cells, whereas CoronaVac boosting led to a small-sized clonal expansion. Furthermore, the utilization of germlines associated with neutralizing antibody were preferentially enriched in recipients with Ad5-nCoV boosting. CONCLUSIONS: Above all, our study gives insights for elaborating the systemic immune landscape of heterologous-boosting COVID-19 immunization by the novel single B cell sorting platform and scRNA/V(D)J-seq technology. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04892459.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the need to understand the immune mechanisms behind heterologous COVID-19 boosting, specifically comparing it to homologous boosting to clarify the underlying immune enhancement process. The objective is to elucidate the systemic immune landscape of heterologous-boosting COVID-19 immunization.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved isolating spike protein binding-specific monoclonal antibodies from participants who received a homologous booster with CoronaVac or a heterologous booster with Ad5-nCoV, following a two-dose CoronaVac priming schedule, using a single B cell sorting platform.
analysis.methods: The researchers verified the neutralization activity of the isolated monoclonal antibodies against SARS-CoV-2 variants, germline gene sequences, and affinity kinetics targeting SARS-CoV-2 NTD/RBD/S1. Additionally, they conducted an in-depth analysis of the immunological response characteristics by integrating single-cell RNA/V(D)J sequencing (scRNA/V(D)J-seq).
analysis.main_results: Heterologous boosting with Ad5-nCoV elicited more mature B cells with higher affinity and activated more abundant immune-related pathways compared to homologous boosting with CoronaVac. Ad5-nCoV boosting expanded unique clonal types of B and T cells, whereas CoronaVac boosting led to a small-sized clonal expansion.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that heterologous boosting with Ad5-nCoV preferentially enriches germlines associated with neutralizing antibodies and activates more mature B cells. The novelty of the study lies in providing insights into the systemic immune landscape of heterologous-boosting COVID-19 immunization using novel single B cell sorting and scRNA/V(D)J-seq technologies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that heterologous boosting strategies may offer superior immune responses compared to homologous boosting, particularly for inactivated vaccines like CoronaVac, which could inform future vaccination strategies and immune profiling approaches.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the immune mechanisms of heterologous versus homologous COVID-19 boosting, comparing Ad5-nCoV with CoronaVac following a two-dose CoronaVac priming schedule. title_zh: COVID-19 疫苗异源与同源加强的系统免疫分析
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Compared with homologous boosting, heterologous boosting with a different COVID-19 vaccine following priming generates stronger antibody responses against severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) as well as variants, particularly for inactivated COVID-19 vaccine(CoronaVac). However, it is still unclear about the potential immune enhancement mechanism underlying heterologous boosting. METHODS: In this study, we isolated spike protein binding-specific monoclonal antibodies at day 180 post a homologous booster with CoronaVac or a heterologous booster with Ad5-nCoV based on two-dose of CoronaVac using the single B cell sorting platform. Subsequently, we verified their neutralization activity to SARS-CoV-2 variants, germline gene sequences and affinity kinetics targeting SARS-CoV-2 NTD/RBD/S1. Additionally, we conducted an in-depth analysis of the immunological response characteristics, by integrating single-cell RNA/V(D)J sequencing(scRNA/ V(D)J-seq). RESULTS: Our study demonstrated that heterologous boosting with Ad5-nCoV elicited more mature B cells with higher affinity and activated more abundant immune-related pathways compared to the homologous boosting with CoronaVac. In addition, Ad5-nCoV boosting expanded unique clonal types of B and T cells, whereas CoronaVac boosting led to a small-sized clonal expansion. Furthermore, the utilization of germlines associated with neutralizing antibody were preferentially enriched in recipients with Ad5-nCoV boosting. CONCLUSIONS: Above all, our study gives insights for elaborating the systemic immune landscape of heterologous-boosting COVID-19 immunization by the novel single B cell sorting platform and scRNA/V(D)J-seq technology. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04892459.

title: Malaria burden and care in hard-to-reach indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon during the COVID-19 pandemic: A mixed-methods study
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with reported disruptions to healthcare delivery and malaria control activities in remote, malaria-endemic indigenous communities with limited access to healthcare. Remote indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon may have been especially vulnerable due to interruptions in malaria surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment. We investigated the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on malaria burden, healthcare access, and community perceptions in hard-to-reach indigenous communities in the Amazonas region of Peru. In malaria-endemic regions, these lessons are particularly important because future health emergencies may similarly affect surveillance, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment activities, potentially reversing gains achieved through malaria control programs. Methods A convergent parallel mixed-methods study was conducted in 2021 and 2022 across four indigenous communities in the Río Santiago district, Amazonas region, Peru. Quantitative data were collected through cross-sectional malaria surveys, and qualitative data were obtained through semi- structured interviews with inhabitants, community health workers, and local health personnel. Malaria infections were detected by microscopy and confirmed by PCR. Factors associated with the occurrence of malaria infection were studied based on a generalized estimating equation (GEE) approach applied to clustered binary outcome data and accounting for repeated observations within participants across study years. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically, and both components were integrated using the Pillar Integration Process framework. Results A total of 514 participants were included. PCR-based malaria prevalence was 17.6% in 2021 and 26.09% in 2022. falciparum prevalence was particularly high in the Alianza Progreso community (2021: 24.19%, 2022: 16.16%) compared to the other studied communities. Previous malaria infection and chills were associated with PCR-confirmed malaria infection. Qualitative findings indicated that COVID-19-related disruptions affected malaria control activities by interrupting diagnosis and treatment availability, reducing community follow-up, and prioritizing COVID-19 response activities over malaria control. Participants also described fear of COVID-19, temporary migration to farm areas, and reliance on herbal medicine during the pandemic. Conclusions The COVID-19 pandemic may have contributed to exacerbated pre-existing challenges to malaria control in remote indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon. Strengthening malaria surveillance, ensuring continuity of diagnosis and treatment, and improving healthcare access in geographically isolated communities will be critical to supporting malaria elimination efforts in Peru. Author summary The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted essential health services worldwide, with potentially greater consequences for remote malaria-endemic communities with limited healthcare access. Indigenous populations in the Peruvian Amazon faced additional challenges due to interruptions in malaria surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, and control activities. We assessed the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on malaria burden and healthcare access in four remote indigenous communities in the Amazonas region of Peru by combining malaria screening with interviews involving community members, community health workers, and healthcare personnel. Our findings showed persistent malaria transmission during the pandemic period, particularly in communities affected by Plasmodium falciparum . Participants reported reduced access to malaria diagnosis and treatment, fewer community follow-up activities, fear of attending health facilities, and changes in healthcare-seeking behaviors. These findings highlight how health emergencies can intensify existing barriers in geographically isolated populations and threaten malaria elimination efforts. Strengthening resilient health systems and ensuring continuity of essential malaria services during future crises will be critical to protect vulnerable communities in the Amazon region.
