title_zh: COVID-19 大流行期间秘鲁亚马逊地区难以到达的土著社区的疟疾负担和护理:一项混合方法研究
source_body_en: Background The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with reported disruptions to healthcare delivery and malaria control activities in remote, malaria-endemic indigenous communities with limited access to healthcare. Remote indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon may have been especially vulnerable due to interruptions in malaria surveillance, diagnosis, and treatment. We investigated the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on malaria burden, healthcare access, and community perceptions in hard-to-reach indigenous communities in the Amazonas region of Peru. In malaria-endemic regions, these lessons are particularly important because future health emergencies may similarly affect surveillance, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment activities, potentially reversing gains achieved through malaria control programs. Methods A convergent parallel mixed-methods study was conducted in 2021 and 2022 across four indigenous communities in the Río Santiago district, Amazonas region, Peru. Quantitative data were collected through cross-sectional malaria surveys, and qualitative data were obtained through semi- structured interviews with inhabitants, community health workers, and local health personnel. Malaria infections were detected by microscopy and confirmed by PCR. Factors associated with the occurrence of malaria infection were studied based on a generalized estimating equation (GEE) approach applied to clustered binary outcome data and accounting for repeated observations within participants across study years. Qualitative data were analyzed thematically, and both components were integrated using the Pillar Integration Process framework. Results A total of 514 participants were included. PCR-based malaria prevalence was 17.6% in 2021 and 26.09% in 2022. falciparum prevalence was particularly high in the Alianza Progreso community (2021: 24.19%, 2022: 16.16%) compared to the other studied communities. Previous malaria infection and chills were associated with PCR-confirmed malaria infection. Qualitative findings indicated that COVID-19-related disruptions affected malaria control activities by interrupting diagnosis and treatment availability, reducing community follow-up, and prioritizing COVID-19 response activities over malaria control. Participants also described fear of COVID-19, temporary migration to farm areas, and reliance on herbal medicine during the pandemic. Conclusions The COVID-19 pandemic may have contributed to exacerbated pre-existing challenges to malaria control in remote indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon. Strengthening malaria surveillance, ensuring continuity of diagnosis and treatment, and improving healthcare access in geographically isolated communities will be critical to supporting malaria elimination efforts in Peru. Author summary The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted essential health services worldwide, with potentially greater consequences for remote malaria-endemic communities with limited healthcare access. Indigenous populations in the Peruvian Amazon faced additional challenges due to interruptions in malaria surveillance, diagnosis, treatment, and control activities. We assessed the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on malaria burden and healthcare access in four remote indigenous communities in the Amazonas region of Peru by combining malaria screening with interviews involving community members, community health workers, and healthcare personnel. Our findings showed persistent malaria transmission during the pandemic period, particularly in communities affected by Plasmodium falciparum . Participants reported reduced access to malaria diagnosis and treatment, fewer community follow-up activities, fear of attending health facilities, and changes in healthcare-seeking behaviors. These findings highlight how health emergencies can intensify existing barriers in geographically isolated populations and threaten malaria elimination efforts. Strengthening resilient health systems and ensuring continuity of essential malaria services during future crises will be critical to protect vulnerable communities in the Amazon region.
abstract_zh: 背景 据报道,在疟疾流行的偏远土著社区,获得医疗服务的机会有限,因此 COVID-19 大流行与医疗服务提供和疟疾控制活动中断有关。由于疟疾监测、诊断和治疗的中断,秘鲁亚马逊地区的偏远土著社区可能特别容易受到影响。我们调查了 COVID-19 大流行对秘鲁亚马逊地区难以到达的土著社区的疟疾负担、医疗保健获取和社区认知的影响。在疟疾流行地区,这些教训尤其重要,因为未来的突发卫生事件可能同样影响监测、诊断、预防和治疗活动,有可能逆转通过疟疾控制计划取得的成果。方法 2021 年和 2022 年在秘鲁亚马逊地区里奥圣地亚哥区的四个土著社区进行了一项收敛并行混合方法研究。定量数据通过横断面疟疾调查收集,定性数据通过对居民、社区卫生工作者和当地卫生人员的半结构化访谈获得。通过显微镜检测疟疾感染并通过PCR确认。基于广义估计方程(GEE)方法研究了与疟疾感染发生相关的因素,该方法应用于聚类二元结果数据,并考虑了研究年份中参与者的重复观察结果。对定性数据进行了主题分析,并使用支柱集成流程框架集成了这两个组件。结果 共有 514 名参与者被纳入。基于 PCR 的疟疾患病率在 2021 年为 17.6%,在 2022 年为 26.09%。与其他研究社区相比,Alianza Progreso 社区的恶性疟疾患病率特别高(2021 年:24.19%,2022 年:16.16%)。既往疟疾感染和发冷与 PCR 确诊的疟疾感染有关。定性研究结果表明,与 COVID-19 相关的干扰影响了疟疾控制活动,因为中断了诊断和治疗的可用性、减少了社区随访以及将 COVID-19 应对活动置于疟疾控制之上。参与者还描述了对 COVID-19 的恐惧、暂时迁移到农场地区以及在大流行期间对草药的依赖。结论 COVID-19 大流行可能加剧了秘鲁亚马逊偏远土著社区疟疾控制方面先前存在的挑战。加强疟疾监测、确保诊断和治疗的连续性以及改善地理偏远社区的医疗保健服务对于支持秘鲁消除疟疾工作至关重要。作者摘要 COVID-19 大流行扰乱了全世界的基本卫生服务,可能对医疗服务有限的偏远疟疾流行社区造成更大的影响。由于疟疾监测、诊断、治疗和控制活动的中断,秘鲁亚马逊地区的土著居民面临着额外的挑战。我们通过将疟疾筛查与对社区成员、社区卫生工作者和医护人员的访谈相结合,评估了 COVID-19 大流行对秘鲁亚马逊地区四个偏远土著社区的疟疾负担和医疗保健获取的影响。我们的研究结果表明,疟疾在大流行期间持续传播,特别是在受恶性疟原虫影响的社区。参与者报告说,获得疟疾诊断和治疗的机会减少,社区后续活动减少,害怕去医疗机构就诊,以及就医行为发生变化。这些发现凸显了突发卫生事件如何加剧地理偏远人群中的现有障碍,并威胁消除疟疾的努力。加强有复原力的卫生系统并确保未来危机期间基本疟疾服务的连续性对于保护亚马逊地区的脆弱社区至关重要。

title: Skin manifestations of primary COVID-19 infection with the omicron variant
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although cutaneous manifestations of COVID-19 have been increasingly documented across earlier variants, the dermatological characteristics specifically associated with the Omicron variant, particularly in the Chinese population, remain insufficiently characterized in the literature. OBJECTIVE: To characterize cutaneous manifestations in patients with primary COVID-19 infection caused by the Omicron variant and corresponding management. METHODS: 94 participants were included in this retrospective analysis, who developed dermatologic symptoms within one month of COVID-19 Omicron Variant infection. RESULTS: Mean age was 38 years old, ranging from 7 to 89; with 66% aged within 25-50. A significantly higher incidence of skin manifestations was reported among females (males vs. females, 1:2.76, p = 0.001). Skin rashes typically appeared three days after the onset of COVID symptoms (ranging between 2-7 days), which were mostly mild to moderate. Common morphological types included wheals, erythema, and papular/papulovesicular eruptions. Generalized rashes occurred in 50% of cases, while localized rashes mainly affected the extremities. Pruritus was the most frequent symptom (>90%), particularly in patients presenting with wheals. Clinical management included topical steroid creams and antiviral treatment for COVID-19. No follow-ups were required for most participants (>95%). CONCLUSION: Skin rashes associated with Omicron variant COVID-19 infection, predominantly affecting young and middle-aged women, are characterized by wheals, erythema, and papular/papulovesicular eruptions. Early identification and management of these cutaneous symptoms should be integrated in the overall treatment plan of Omicron variant COVID-19 infection.

title: PI3K gene variants are associated with elevated IL-6 levels and COVID-19 severe outcomes in a multicenter study
abstract: The COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2 has resulted in widely variable clinical outcomes. The virus relies on host metabolic pathways particularly the PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis, which regulate cell survival, metabolism, and viral replication. Genetic variants whitin this pathway may influence disease severity. This study evaluated variants in PI3K genes among 216 mild and 291 severe COVID-19 patients, focusing on rs3730089 (PIK3R1), rs785468 (PIK3R3), and rs11121484 (PIK3CD). Genotypes were evaluted in peripheral blood samples, inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF) were measured in plasma samples and immune cell profiles were assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The C allele of rs11121484 was associated with susceptibility to severe COVID-19, while rs785468 and rs3730089 were correlated with higher mortality risk. The presence of multiple risk alleles showed a cumulative effect on disease outcome. Patients with the GG genotype of rs3730089 had increased IL-6 levels, and carriers of risk alleles displayed reduced non-classic monocytes and CD4 + memory T cells. These findings indicate that PI3K single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) may exacerbate inflammation and immune dysregulation in COVID-19, contributing to severe outcomes. Overall, these results highlight a potential pathological role for PI3K SNVs in driving hyperinflammation in COVID-19 patients and may contributes to predicting the severe outcome of COVID-19 and better disease prognosis.

title_zh: 一项多中心研究显示 PI3K 基因变异与 IL-6 水平升高和 COVID-19 严重后果相关
source_body_en: The COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2 has resulted in widely variable clinical outcomes. The virus relies on host metabolic pathways particularly the PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis, which regulate cell survival, metabolism, and viral replication. Genetic variants whitin this pathway may influence disease severity. This study evaluated variants in PI3K genes among 216 mild and 291 severe COVID-19 patients, focusing on rs3730089 (PIK3R1), rs785468 (PIK3R3), and rs11121484 (PIK3CD). Genotypes were evaluted in peripheral blood samples, inflammatory cytokines (IL-6 and TNF) were measured in plasma samples and immune cell profiles were assessed in peripheral blood mononuclear cells. The C allele of rs11121484 was associated with susceptibility to severe COVID-19, while rs785468 and rs3730089 were correlated with higher mortality risk. The presence of multiple risk alleles showed a cumulative effect on disease outcome. Patients with the GG genotype of rs3730089 had increased IL-6 levels, and carriers of risk alleles displayed reduced non-classic monocytes and CD4 + memory T cells. These findings indicate that PI3K single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) may exacerbate inflammation and immune dysregulation in COVID-19, contributing to severe outcomes. Overall, these results highlight a potential pathological role for PI3K SNVs in driving hyperinflammation in COVID-19 patients and may contributes to predicting the severe outcome of COVID-19 and better disease prognosis.
abstract_zh: 由 SARS-CoV-2 引起的 COVID-19 导致临床结果差异很大。该病毒依赖宿主代谢途径,特别是 PI3K/AKT/mTOR 轴,调节细胞存活、代谢和病毒复制。该途径中的遗传变异可能会影响疾病的严重程度。本研究评估了 216 名轻度和 291 名重症 COVID-19 患者的 PI3K 基因变异,重点关注 rs3730089 (PIK3R1)、rs785468 (PIK3R3) 和 rs11121484 (PIK3CD)。评估外周血样本中的基因型,测量血浆样本中的炎性细胞因子(IL-6和TNF),并评估外周血单核细胞中的免疫细胞谱。rs11121484 的 C 等位基因与严重 COVID-19 的易感性相关,而 rs785468 和 rs3730089 与较高的死亡风险相关。多个风险等位基因的存在显示出对疾病结果的累积影响。rs3730089 GG 基因型患者的 IL-6 水平升高,风险等位基因携带者的非经典单核细胞和 CD4 + 记忆 T 细胞减少。这些发现表明 PI3K 单核苷酸变异 (SNV) 可能会加剧 COVID-19 中的炎症和免疫失调,从而导致严重的后果。总体而言,这些结果强调了 PI3K SNV 在驱动 COVID-19 患者过度炎症中的潜在病理作用,并可能有助于预测 COVID-19 的严重后果和更好的疾病预后。

title: Investigating respiratory infection as a post-COVID-19 condition using a large passive surveillance cohort from Track PCC.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study examined risk factors for post-COVID respiratory infection using data from the Tracking the Burden, Distribution, Impact of Tracking Post-COVID-19 Conditions in Diverse Populations for Children, Adolescents, Adults (Track PCC) passive surveillance cohort. METHODS: This retrospective study included adult Temple Health patients in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania with SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) infections from March 2020 to December 2022 and ≥ 90 days follow-up. COVID-19 infection was identified via laboratory testing, billing codes, or clinical documentation. The primary outcome was post-COVID respiratory infection identified by billing codes. Predictors included social, clinical, and COVID-related correlates. Adjusted logistic regression models were used on 17,539 complete cases and multiple imputed datasets (n = 45,513) with SuperMICE. RESULTS: In complete-case analysis, uninsured coverage, Alpha variant, total comorbidities, and hospitalization were associated with lower odds of respiratory post-COVID conditions (ORs: 0.02-0.99). Dual Medicare/Medicaid and current smokers, increased odds (ORs: 1.33-1.58). Imputed analyses showed consistent results with and additionally observed higher odds of respiratory infection among those with Medicaid and higher number of vaccinations, and lower odds among those of any non-white race, Hispanic ethnicity. CONCLUSIONS: Temple Track PCC findings identify high-risk populations and underscore the utility of advanced imputation in surveillance-based research.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究使用来自跟踪儿童、青少年、成人不同人群中 COVID-19 后状况的负担、分布和影响 (Track PCC) 被动监测队列的数据,研究了 COVID 后呼吸道感染的危险因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究纳入了宾夕法尼亚州费城坦普尔健康中心 2020 年 3 月至 2022 年 12 月期间感染 SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) 的成年患者,并进行了 ≥ 90 天的随访。
elements_zh.methods: COVID-19 感染是通过实验室检测、账单代码或临床文件确定的。主要结果是通过帐单代码识别的新冠肺炎后呼吸道感染。使用 SuperMICE 对 17,539 个完整病例和多个估算数据集 (n = 45,513) 使用调整后的逻辑回归模型。
elements_zh.main_results: 在完整病例分析中,未投保范围、Alpha 变异、总合并症和住院治疗与新冠肺炎后呼吸道疾病发生率较低相关(OR:0.02-0.99)。双重医疗保险/医疗补助和当前吸烟者的几率增加(OR:1.33-1.58)。估算分析显示,结果一致,并且还观察到,在接受医疗补助和疫苗接种次数较多的人群中,呼吸道感染的几率较高,而在任何非白人种族、西班牙裔人群中,呼吸道感染的几率较低。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: Temple Track PCC 的研究结果确定了高风险人群,并强调了高级插补在基于监测的研究中的实用性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可以为针对高危人群的针对性干预措施提供信息,并改进新冠疫情后状况的监测方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对结果识别的计费代码的依赖而受到限制,但多重插补的使用增强了证据。

title: Association of COVID-19 vaccination with improved treatment adherence in patients with schizophrenia: A propensity score-matched cohort study
abstract: People with schizophrenia are a high-priority group for COVID-19 vaccination. However, large-scale data on the real-world clinical impact of vaccination in this vulnerable population is limited. We aimed to evaluate the association of COVID-19 vaccination with treatment adherence, psychiatric stability, and SARS-CoV-2 infection risk in patients with schizophrenia. We conducted a nationwide, retrospective, propensity score-matched cohort study (study period: December 1, 2019-December 31, 2022) using linked data from the National Health Insurance Service and Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency databases in South Korea. We identified patients with schizophrenia aged 19-64 years and stratified them into vaccinated (three doses) and unvaccinated groups. A 1:1 propensity score matching was performed. The primary outcomes were schizophrenia-related hospitalization and emergency department visits. Key secondary outcomes included medication adherence and diagnosed SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study cohort comprised 4629 pairs (N = 9258). No significant between-group differences were observed in the rates of schizophrenia-related hospitalization or emergency department visits. The vaccinated group showed a significantly smaller decline in medication adherence compared with the unvaccinated group. Counter-intuitively, the vaccinated group had a significantly higher rate of diagnosed SARS-CoV-2 infection, a finding most plausibly attributable to ascertainment bias rather than reduced vaccine efficacy. COVID-19 vaccination was not associated with psychiatric destabilization but was associated with significantly improved treatment adherence. Our study indicates that vaccination may play a supportive role in maintaining clinical continuity for individuals with schizophrenia.

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,COVID-19 疫苗接种可以支持精神分裂症的临床连续性,可能为这一高优先群体的疫苗接种策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到与直觉相反的较高感染率的限制,这最有可能归因于确定偏差,而不是疫苗功效降低。由于倾向评分匹配和大样本量,证据强度中等。

title: Physical activity in social contexts during the COVID-19 pandemic: a latent transition analysis
abstract: Background While physical activity behaviours have been explored during the COVID-19 pandemic, little is known about the social contexts in which physical activity took place during this time of crisis. The purpose of this longitudinal study was to explore the physical activity-related social contexts in which young people (aged 15-24) engaged during the first two years of the COVID-19 pandemic in Ontario, Canada. Specific objectives included identifying: (1) how patterns of engagement in social contexts changed over time; and (2) demographic/descriptive predictors of social context-related class membership. Methods Online surveys were completed from: (1) July-September 2020; (2) November 2020-January 2021; and (3) July 2021-January 2022. Data on gender, living situation, physical activity, and physical activity-related social contexts were collected. Latent transition analysis was conducted to determine how participant's social contexts changed over time and chi-squared tests were used to assess predictors of latent profile membership. Results Participants (n = 328; M age = 22.95) were categorized into three latent classes: 1 = mainly active alone; 2 = limited physical activity in all contexts; and 3 = mainly active with others. At Time 1, nearly 70.0% of participants were in Class 1; at Times 2 and 3, most participants (62.1% and 53.6%, respectively) were in Class 2. From Times 1-2, most participants (67.1%) transitioned from Class 1 to Class 2. From Times 2-3, more than 75.0% of participants remained in their respective classes. Class membership was associated with various predictors at different time points. Conclusion Results underscore the need to promote participation in a variety of physical activity-related social contexts, particularly during times of crisis.

abstract_zh: 背景 虽然在 COVID-19 大流行期间人们对身体活动行为进行了探索,但人们对危机期间发生身体活动的社会背景知之甚少。这项纵向研究的目的是探讨加拿大安大略省 COVID-19 大流行的头两年年轻人(15-24 岁)参与的与身体活动相关的社会环境。具体目标包括确定:(1)社会环境中的参与模式如何随时间变化;(2) 与社会背景相关的阶层成员资格的人口统计/描述性预测因素。方法 在线调查完成时间为:(1)2020年7月-9月;(2)2020年11月-2021年1月;(3)2021年7月-2022年1月。收集性别、生活状况、身体活动以及与身体活动相关的社会背景的数据。进行潜在转变分析以确定参与者的社会背景如何随时间变化,并使用卡方检验来评估潜在概况成员资格的预测因素。结果 参与者(n = 328;M 年龄 = 22.95)被分为三个潜在类别:1 = 主要单独活动;2 = 单独活动。2 = 在所有情况下体力活动均有限;3 = 主要与他人交往。在时间 1,近 70.0% 的参与者属于 1 类;在第 2 次和第 3 次,大多数参与者(分别为 62.1% 和 53.6%)属于第 2 类。从第 1-2 次,大多数参与者(67.1%)从第 1 类过渡到第 2 类。从第 2-3 次,超过 75.0% 的参与者留在各自的班级。班级成员资格与不同时间点的各种预测因素相关。结论 结果强调需要促进参与各种与身体活动相关的社会环境,特别是在危机时期。

title: Trauma Nurses' Perceptions of Burnout, Value, and Administrative Interventions During COVID-19
abstract: BACKGROUND Nurse burnout during COVID-19 has been well studied; however, limited research exists on the impact of hospital administrators' interventions on trauma nurses' perceptions of burnout and value during staffing crises. OBJECTIVE To examine contributors to burnout and explore administrative interventions affecting trauma nurses' perceived value during COVID-19. METHODS This exploratory, sequential mixed-methods study was conducted in 2 phases at a Level II trauma center in the western United States from January 2022 to January 2024. In phase 1, qualitative data from 13 semi-structured interviews with trauma nurses and administrators informed development of a cross-sectional survey. In phase 2, the resulting 50-item survey was distributed at the trauma center, through the Society of Trauma Nurses list serv, and at the 2023 conference. RESULTS Of 204 individuals who initiated the survey, 126 (62%) completed it (local: 45/69, 65%; national: 81/135, 60%). A response rate could not be calculated because of the multimodal distribution method. Exhaustion from an increased workload was the most reported burnout factor (n = 115/123, 93%). Distress from crisis standards of care ranked second (n = 112/124, 90%). Nurses felt most valued from financial incentives (n = 92/123, 75%) and a responsive administration (n = 79/123, 64%). Nurses felt least valued from "Healthcare Heroes" campaigns (n = 75/124, 60%). Nurses satisfied with administrative support had lower odds of reporting burnout from administrative delays (OR, 0.49; 95% CI, 0.31-0.85; p < .01). CONCLUSIONS Administrative approaches that reduce workload, prioritize responsiveness, and emphasize higher wages may improve nurse perceptions of value and mitigate burnout during staffing crises, whereas symbolic gestures such as "Healthcare Heroes" should be avoided.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines perceptions of burnout, value, and administrative interventions among trauma nurses during COVID-19 staffing crises, focusing on contributors to burnout and the impact of hospital administrators' actions on nurses' perceived value.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This exploratory, sequential mixed-methods study included two phases: qualitative interviews with 13 trauma nurses and administrators to inform a 50-item survey, followed by a cross-sectional survey distributed at a Level II trauma center, via the Society of Trauma Nurses listserv, and at a 2023 conference from January 2022 to January 2024. The survey had 126 complete responses (62% completion rate) from 204 initiators, with no calculable response rate due to multimodal distribution.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Exhaustion from increased workload was the most reported burnout factor (93%), followed by distress from crisis standards of care (90%). analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study did not report the representativeness of the sample or potential selection bias introduced by multimodal survey distribution. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prioritize research on the long-term effectiveness and sustainability of administrative interventions such as financial incentives and responsive administration in mitigating burnout. elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究没有报告样本的代表性或多模式调查分布引入的潜在选择偏差。该审查并未涉及财政激励或行政响应等干预措施在不同医疗保健环境中是否可持续或可扩展。

title: COVID-19-associated mucormycosis: the rise and fall of an epidemic within a pandemic - a systematic review of 1,482 cases (2019-2025)
abstract: ABSTRACT During the COVID-19 pandemic, an unprecedented outbreak of mucormycosis affected tens of thousands of patients, mainly in India. This study reviewed the available published cases up to 2022 and updated the epidemiological curve up to November 2025. PRISMA-guided systematic review of PubMed, Embase, and SciELO (Dec. 2022), supplemented by official reports and cohort studies published until 2025. We analyzed 1,482 cases from 39 studies (90.8% conducted in India; 69.7% male individuals; mean age 52 years). Diabetes mellitus was present in >78% of patients, and 64.3% received corticosteroids. Rhino-orbital (40.7%) and rhino-orbito-cerebral (33.9%) were the dominant forms of mucormycosis. Amphotericin B was used in 49.5% of cases, and surgical debridement in 55.5%. The mortality rate was 25%. After 2022, the incidence collapsed globally: India dropped from >47,000 cases in 2021 to <100 cases/year; Europe, the Middle East, and Latin America reported zero outbreaks in 2024-2025. COVID-19-associated mucormycosis represented a major opportunistic infection during the acute phase of the pandemic. Although its incidence declined markedly after widespread vaccination implementation, improved corticosteroid use, and better glycemic control, it remains a serious and life-threatening condition in vulnerable populations. The findings highlight important risk factors, clinical challenges, and management considerations that remain relevant to inform current clinical practice and future post-pandemic scenarios.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines COVID-19-associated mucormycosis, focusing on the pathogen *Mucorales*, the disease mucormycosis, human hosts, and populations affected during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly in India. The central question addresses the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and outcomes of this opportunistic infection within the context of the pandemic.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a PRISMA-guided systematic review of PubMed, Embase, and SciELO databases up to December 2022, supplemented by official reports and cohort studies published until 2025. The review analyzed 1,482 cases from 39 studies, with 90.8% conducted in India, involving 69.7% male individuals and a mean age of 52 years.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review identifies diabetes mellitus as a predominant risk factor (>78% of patients) and corticosteroid use in 64.3% of cases. Rhino-orbital (40.7%) and rhino-orbito-cerebral (33.9%) forms were the most common clinical presentations. Amphotericin B was administered in 49.5% of cases, and surgical debridement in 55.5%, with an overall mortality rate of 25%. Post-2022, the incidence of COVID-19-associated mucormycosis declined sharply, with India reporting <100 cases/year and no outbreaks in Europe, the Middle East, or Latin America by 2024-2025.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report the specific criteria used to define COVID-19-associated mucormycosis cases or the diagnostic methods employed across studies. analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings underscore the need for standardized diagnostic criteria and reporting for COVID-19-associated mucormycosis to improve surveillance and clinical management. Further research is required to elucidate the factors contributing to the decline in incidence, particularly the roles of vaccination, corticosteroid stewardship, and glycemic control. Clinicians should maintain vigilance for mucormycosis in vulnerable populations, including those with uncontrolled diabetes or recent corticosteroid use.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines COVID-19-associated mucormycosis, an opportunistic fungal infection that surged during the pandemic, particularly in India. elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是 PRISMA 指导下对截至 2022 年 12 月的 PubMed、Embase 和 SciELO 数据库进行的系统评价,并辅以截至 2025 年发布的官方报告和队列研究。该评价分析了 39 项研究的 1,482 例病例,其中 90.8% 在印度进行,涉及 69.7% 的男性个体,平均年龄 52 岁。

elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告用于定义与 COVID-19 相关的毛霉菌病病例的具体标准或各研究中采用的诊断方法。此外,它没有解决病例报告或印度以外地区数据完整性的潜在偏差。2022 年之后发病率迅速下降的机制仍未解决。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调需要制定与 COVID-19 相关的毛霉菌病的标准化诊断标准和报告,以改善监测和临床管理。需要进一步的研究来阐明导致发病率下降的因素,特别是疫苗接种、皮质类固醇管理和血糖控制的作用。临床医生应对易感人群中的毛霉菌病保持警惕,包括糖尿病未得到控制或近期使用皮质类固醇的人群。

title_zh: COVID-19 相关毛霉菌病:大流行中流行病的兴衰——对 1,482 例病例的系统回顾(2019-2025 年)
source_body_en: ABSTRACT During the COVID-19 pandemic, an unprecedented outbreak of mucormycosis affected tens of thousands of patients, mainly in India. This study reviewed the available published cases up to 2022 and updated the epidemiological curve up to November 2025. PRISMA-guided systematic review of PubMed, Embase, and SciELO (Dec. 2022), supplemented by official reports and cohort studies published until 2025. We analyzed 1,482 cases from 39 studies (90.8% conducted in India; 69.7% male individuals; mean age 52 years). Diabetes mellitus was present in >78% of patients, and 64.3% received corticosteroids. Rhino-orbital (40.7%) and rhino-orbito-cerebral (33.9%) were the dominant forms of mucormycosis. Amphotericin B was used in 49.5% of cases, and surgical debridement in 55.5%. The mortality rate was 25%. After 2022, the incidence collapsed globally: India dropped from >47,000 cases in 2021 to <100 cases/year; Europe, the Middle East, and Latin America reported zero outbreaks in 2024-2025. COVID-19-associated mucormycosis represented a major opportunistic infection during the acute phase of the pandemic. Although its incidence declined markedly after widespread vaccination implementation, improved corticosteroid use, and better glycemic control, it remains a serious and life-threatening condition in vulnerable populations. The findings highlight important risk factors, clinical challenges, and management considerations that remain relevant to inform current clinical practice and future post-pandemic scenarios.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了与 COVID-19 相关的毛霉菌病,重点关注病原体 *毛霉菌目 *、毛霉菌病、人类宿主以及在 COVID-19 大流行期间受影响的人群,特别是在印度。核心问题涉及大流行背景下这种机会性感染的流行病学、临床特征和结果。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是 PRISMA 指导下对截至 2022 年 12 月的 PubMed、Embase 和 SciELO 数据库进行的系统评价,并辅以截至 2025 年发布的官方报告和队列研究。该评价分析了 39 项研究的 1,482 例病例,其中 90.8% 在印度进行,涉及 69.7% 的男性个体,平均年龄 52 岁。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述确定糖尿病(>78%的患者)和皮质类固醇使用(64.3%的病例)为主要风险因素。鼻眶型(40.7%)和鼻眶脑型(33.9%)是最常见的临床表现。49.5%的病例接受了两性霉素B治疗,55.5%进行了手术清创,总体死亡率为25%。2022年后,COVID-19相关曲霉病的发病率急剧下降,印度报告<100例/年,到2024-2025年欧洲、中东或拉丁美洲无爆发。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告用于定义与 COVID-19 相关的毛霉菌病病例的具体标准或各研究中采用的诊断方法。此外,它没有解决病例报告或印度以外地区数据完整性的潜在偏差。2022 年之后发病率迅速下降的机制仍未解决。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调需要制定与 COVID-19 相关的毛霉菌病的标准化诊断标准和报告,以改善监测和临床管理。需要进一步的研究来阐明导致发病率下降的因素,特别是疫苗接种、皮质类固醇管理和血糖控制的作用。临床医生应对易感人群中的毛霉菌病保持警惕,包括糖尿病未得到控制或近期使用皮质类固醇的人群。

title: The COVID-19 Pandemic and Changes in Cancer Screening Disparities from 2015 to 2023: An NSHAP Survey Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND From 1990 to 2020, cancer screening rates in the United States steadily rose, but disparities persisted. Cancer screening was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic, possibly worsening disparities. OBJECTIVE We utilized a longitudinal cohort of age-eligible adults to examine pre-pandemic (2015-16) and late-pandemic (2021-23) cancer screening rates to evaluate health disparities. DESIGN This is a study of participants who completed National Social Life, Health, and Aging Project (NSHAP) surveys in 2015-16 and 2021-23. We used univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses to measure differences by age, gender, race and ethnicity, education level, marital status, and income in screening for colorectal, prostate and breast cancer. PARTICIPANTS We studied data from 2,585 NSHAP participants who completed both surveys. MAIN MEASURES Self-reported past-year colorectal, breast, and prostate cancer screening rates completed with colonoscopies, mammograms, and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing, respectively. KEY RESULTS The proportion of respondents completing colonoscopies, mammograms, and PSA testing did not change across surveys. Younger individuals (aged < 60) had lower mammogram rates in 2015-16 (52.8% vs. 62.9%, p = 0.04) and lower PSA testing in both surveys (37.0% vs. 53.5%, p < 0.001 and 34.3% vs. Hispanic respondents had the lowest colonoscopy screening rates in 2015-16 (12.1%, p = 0.006) and 2021-23 (7.6%, p = 0.002), and Black women had the highest for mammograms in 2015-16 (65.3%, p = 0.04). Non-partnered men had lower PSA testing than partnered men in both surveys (p = 0.02 and p = 0.005). All screening rates were lower for those with lower incomes in 2015-16 (p < 0.05 for all). Analyses did not show significant demographic differences in screening rates over time. CONCLUSIONS Overall population cancer screening rates remained consistent from 2015-16 to 2021-23. Demographic differences in cancer screening rates persisted, with no subgroups disproportionately affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. Targeted outreach is needed for demographic subgroups such as Hispanic individuals with persistently low colorectal cancer screening rates.

title: Recent COVID-19 Vaccination Before Glioblastoma Surgery Is Associated With Longer Survival
abstract: Abstract Background Glioblastoma remains resistant to most immune-based therapies. Surgery may create a perioperative window in which systemic immune activation and tumor antigen release intersect. We evaluated whether COVID-19 vaccination shortly before first glioblastoma surgery was associated with survival. Methods We performed a retrospective single-center cohort study of adults with newly diagnosed glioblastoma undergoing initial biopsy or resection from 2021 to 2025. The primary exposure was documented COVID-19 vaccination within 100 days before first tumor surgery. Overall survival was analyzed from surgery using Kaplan–Meier and Cox models, with 1:1 propensity matching and sensitivity analyses addressing treatment completion, calendar time, surgical selection, steroid exposure, immune-cell variables, COVID severity, and negative-control vaccination. Results The cohort included 187 patients: 64 perioperatively vaccinated and 123 non-perioperative comparators. Among vaccinated patients, 59/64 (92.2%) received mRNA vaccines; median vaccination-to-surgery interval was 81 days (IQR 71–90). Median overall survival was 743 days in vaccinated patients versus 318 days in comparators (unmatched HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.30–0.76; p=0.002). After 1:1 matching, median survival was 743 versus 349 days (HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.34–0.80). Sensitivity analyses accounting for adjuvant therapy, surgery year, extent of resection, steroid exposure, immune-cell measures, and COVID hospitalization were directionally consistent. Influenza vaccination was not associated with survival. Conclusions COVID-19 vaccination within 100 days before first glioblastoma surgery was associated with longer overall survival. These findings identify perioperative vaccination timing as a potentially relevant and modifiable variable in glioblastoma outcomes.

title: Health-related quality of life profiles and trajectories of patients with post COVID-19 condition: a latent Markov model.
abstract: Background The aim of this study was to identify subgroups with similar health states based on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) profile (i.e. differences in affected dimensions and severity of problems per dimension) among PCC patients, to examine transitions between these subgroups over time, and to examine the association with sociodemographic and medical characteristics. Methods In this longitudinal cohort study, data from 5,737 PCC patients, collected through two online surveys, were analysed using a latent Markov model. Dichotomized HRQoL scores per EQ-5D-5L dimension were used as indicators to determine latent states and covariates were added into the model. Results A model with six latent states was selected. The largest state, consisting of 31% of respondents, was characterized by a high probability of problems on all dimensions, whereas the smallest state (7%) was characterized by a low probability of problems on all dimensions, except usual activities. The remaining four states were all characterized by a high probability of problems on usual activities and pain/discomfort, but differed based on the probability of problems on the dimensions mobility, self-care and anxiety/depression. The probability of transitioning to a different state was low, with states with fewer affected dimensions being most stable. Women, younger respondents, those with a lower educational level, and those with comorbidity were more likely to be in states with more affected dimensions. Conclusions The identification of different HRQoL profiles shows that there is substantial heterogeneity in the HRQoL dimensions that are affected and in observed changes between two measurement points.

abstract_zh: 背景 本研究的目的是根据 PCC 患者的健康相关生活质量 (HRQoL) 概况(即受影响维度和每个维度问题严重程度的差异)来识别具有相似健康状况的亚组,检查这些亚组之间随时间的转变,并检查与社会人口学和医学特征的关联。方法 在这项纵向队列研究中,使用潜在马尔可夫模型对通过两次在线调查收集的 5,737 名 PCC 患者的数据进行了分析。每个 EQ-5D-5L 维度的二分 HRQoL 分数用作确定潜在状态的指标,并将协变量添加到模型中。结果选择了具有六个潜在状态的模型。最大的州(由 31% 的受访者组成)的特点是在所有维度上出现问题的概率都很高,而最小的州(7%)的特点是除了日常活动之外,在所有维度上出现问题的概率都很低。其余四种状态的特征都是在日常活动和疼痛/不适方面出现问题的可能性很高,但在活动能力、自我护理和焦虑/抑郁方面出现问题的概率有所不同。转换到不同状态的概率很低,受影响维度较少的状态最稳定。女性、年轻受访者、教育水平较低的受访者以及患有合并症的受访者更有可能处于受影响程度更大的州。结论 不同 HRQoL 概况的识别表明,受影响的 HRQoL 维度以及两个测量点之间观察到的变化存在显着的异质性。

title: Community-Engaged Respondent-Driven Sampling: The California Pacific Islander Well-Being and COVID-19 Economic Survey, 2024.
abstract: To describe how community engagement combined with respondent-driven sampling (RDS) enabled timely documentation of the mental health and socioeconomic impacts of COVID-19 on California's Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander (NHPI) adult population. The California Pacific Islander Well-Being and COVID-19 Economic Survey (CAPIWAVES) was a collaboration between NHPI community-based organizations and academic researchers who sampled 929 NHPI adults in California from January to May 2024. The initial respondents were composed of a convenience sample of 58 CHamoru, Fijian, Marshallese, Native Hawaiian, Sāmoan, and Tongan respondents in Northern, Central, and Southern California, who referred up to 4 others. Compared with the American Community Survey, CAPIWAVES RDS estimates differed. We reported initial data findings to NHPI community members in June 2024 in an online webinar. In April 2025, we released a report with the analyzed CAPIWAVES data, with community-generated recommendations for policy, programming, and research. Although data were not population-representative, community-engaged RDS was an efficient method for collecting and disseminating needed data for minoritized populations. ( Am J Public Health . Published online ahead of print July 16, 2026:e1-e12. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308517).

abstract_zh: 描述社区参与与受访者驱动抽样 (RDS) 相结合如何及时记录 COVID-19 对加州夏威夷原住民和太平洋岛民 (NHPI) 成年人口的心理健康和社会经济影响。加州太平洋岛民福祉和 COVID-19 经济调查 (CAPIWAVES) 是 NHPI 社区组织和学术研究人员之间的一项合作,他们于 2024 年 1 月至 5 月对加州的 929 名 NHPI 成年人进行了抽样调查。最初的受访者由来自加州北部、中部和南部的 58 名查莫罗人、斐济人、马绍尔人、夏威夷原住民、萨摩亚人和汤加人的方便样本组成,他们还提到了另外 4 人。与美国社区调查相比,CAPIWAVES RDS 的估计有所不同。我们于 2024 年 6 月在一次在线网络研讨会上向 NHPI 社区成员报告了初步数据发现。2025 年 4 月,我们发布了一份报告,其中包含分析后的 CAPIWAVES 数据,以及社区针对政策、规划和研究提出的建议。尽管数据不具有人口代表性,但社区参与的 RDS 是收集和传播少数群体所需数据的有效方法。(《Am J Public Health》。2026 年 7 月 16 日印刷前在线发布:e1-e12。https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2026.308517)。

title: Epidemics and Nigerian Society: Lessons from Smallpox to COVID-19
abstract: Nigeria's struggle with epidemic disease, from colonial-era smallpox campaigns to the COVID-19 pandemic, provides a century-long record of how a society has navigated between biomedical intervention and lived social experience. Historical and contemporary disease outbreaks in Nigeria are rarely studied as a connected sequence. Scholarship isolates each epidemic within its own disciplinary environment, distorting patterns of governance, culture, and social response that repeat across time. This paper addressed that challenge through a comparative historical analysis of four epidemic moments in Nigeria which are smallpox and other pre-contemporary epidemics such as, HIV/AIDS, the 2014 Ebola outbreak, and COVID-19. The paper draws on colonial and postcolonial health records, government and multilateral reports, and peer-reviewed literature. It traced how institutional legacies, public trust in the state, and cultural frameworks of illness have redefined each successive epidemic. The analysis found a strong path dependency which is are mechanisms improvised during the smallpox and polio campaigns. On the other hand, community engagement, traditional leadership, decentralized surveillance, reemerged as decisive factors behind Nigeria's most effective interventions. Notable among this was the Ebola containment, while their erosion correlates with weaker outcomes in the HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 responses. The paper closes with recommendations for repositioning community-centred, culturally literate governance into Nigeria's epidemic preparedness strive.
journal: Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities Research Fundamentals

title_zh: 流行病与尼日利亚社会:从天花到 COVID-19 的教训
source_body_en: Nigeria's struggle with epidemic disease, from colonial-era smallpox campaigns to the COVID-19 pandemic, provides a century-long record of how a society has navigated between biomedical intervention and lived social experience. Historical and contemporary disease outbreaks in Nigeria are rarely studied as a connected sequence. Scholarship isolates each epidemic within its own disciplinary environment, distorting patterns of governance, culture, and social response that repeat across time. This paper addressed that challenge through a comparative historical analysis of four epidemic moments in Nigeria which are smallpox and other pre-contemporary epidemics such as, HIV/AIDS, the 2014 Ebola outbreak, and COVID-19. The paper draws on colonial and postcolonial health records, government and multilateral reports, and peer-reviewed literature. It traced how institutional legacies, public trust in the state, and cultural frameworks of illness have redefined each successive epidemic. The analysis found a strong path dependency which is are mechanisms improvised during the smallpox and polio campaigns. On the other hand, community engagement, traditional leadership, decentralized surveillance, reemerged as decisive factors behind Nigeria's most effective interventions. Notable among this was the Ebola containment, while their erosion correlates with weaker outcomes in the HIV/AIDS and COVID-19 responses. The paper closes with recommendations for repositioning community-centred, culturally literate governance into Nigeria's epidemic preparedness strive.
abstract_zh: 尼日利亚与流行病的斗争,从殖民时代的天花运动到 COVID-19 大流行,提供了一个世纪以来社会如何在生物医学干预和生活社会经验之间导航的记录。尼日利亚历史上和当代的疾病爆发很少被作为一个相互关联的序列来研究。学术将每种流行病隔离在其自身的学科环境中,扭曲了随时间重复出现的治理、文化和社会反应模式。本文通过对尼日利亚的四个流行病时刻(天花和其他前当代流行病,例如艾滋病毒/艾滋病、2014 年埃博拉疫情和 COVID-19)进行比较历史分析来应对这一挑战。该论文借鉴了殖民时期和后殖民时期的健康记录、政府和多边报告以及同行评审的文献。它追溯了制度遗产、公众对国家的信任以及疾病的文化框架如何重新定义了每一次连续的流行病。分析发现,存在很强的路径依赖性,这是天花和脊髓灰质炎运动期间临时建立的机制。另一方面,社区参与、传统领导、分散监控重新成为尼日利亚最有效干预措施背后的决定性因素。其中值得注意的是埃博拉病毒的遏制,而其侵蚀与艾滋病毒/艾滋病和 COVID-19 应对措施的疲软结果相关。该文件最后提出了将以社区为中心、具有文化素养的治理重新定位到尼日利亚流行病防备工作中的建议。

title: The CCR2 inflammatory pathway is a target for improving severe disease and pulmonary inflammation in experimental COVID-19
abstract: Abstract SARS-CoV2 can induce an acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), provoked by a dysregulated hyper-inflammatory pulmonary immune response. Here we used the keratinocyte-18 humanized angiotensin converting enzyme-2 (K18-hACE2) mouse model of SARS-CoV2, where expression of the CoV2 spike protein receptor, hACE-2, is restricted to epithelia, to characterize inflammatory pulmonary immune responses post-intranasal infections with the delta isolate SARS-CoV2(Δ B.1.617.2). Immune-profiling by focused transcript analysis, inflammatory protein array, and multi-color flow cytometry, confirmed that clinically relevant markers of COVID-19 (IL-6, GM-CSF, neutrophils, inflammatory monocytes) were significantly elevated in lungs of mice at day 5 post-infection and that remdesivir anti-viral active metabolite (GS441524) treatment significantly modified SARS-CoV2Δ viral loads and pulmonary-specific inflammation. Chemokine ligands of CCR2 (CCL2/7/8) were amongst the top 5% upregulated pulmonary transcripts in a focused human infection response array to SARS-CoV2Δ. CCL2 was confirmed as elevated in protein assays in SARS-CoV2Δ infected lungs. To address functional relevance of the CCR2 pathway of inflammatory cell recruitment to the lungs mediating disease, mice were administered with anti-CCR2 antibody daily at point of infection for up to six days. Anti-CCR2 treated mice showed significant improved welfare scores, were protected from weight loss, modified myeloid pneumonitis, and displayed significantly blunted cytokine and chemokine response in the lungs, despite not affecting pulmonary viral loads. Our data supports therapeutic benefit of modifying CCR2-dependent cell recruitment in the treatment of viral-induced ARDS.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 摘要 SARS-CoV2 可诱发急性呼吸窘迫综合征 (ARDS),这是由过度炎症性肺部免疫反应失调引起的。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 提供的证据没有明确说明研究设计、设置或研究人群。
elements_zh.methods: 在这里,我们使用 SARS-CoV2 的角质形成细胞 18 人源化血管紧张素转换酶 2 (K18-hACE2) 小鼠模型,其中 CoV2 刺突蛋白受体 hACE-2 的表达仅限于上皮细胞,以表征 Delta 分离株 SARS-CoV2 (Δ B.1.617.2) 鼻内感染后的炎症性肺部免疫反应。
elements_zh.main_results: 抗CCR2治疗的小鼠表现出显着改善的福利评分,免受体重减轻和改良性骨髓性肺炎的影响,并且显示出肺部细胞因子和趋化因子反应显着减弱,尽管不影响肺部病毒载量。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们的数据支持修改 CCR2 依赖性细胞募集在治疗病毒诱导的 ARDS 中的治疗益处。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 通过聚焦转录物分析、炎症蛋白阵列和多色流式细胞术进行的免疫分析证实,感染后第 5 天,小鼠肺部的 COVID-19 临床相关标记物(IL-6、GM-CSF、中性粒细胞、炎症单核细胞)显着升高,并且瑞德西韦抗病毒活性代谢物 (GS441524) 治疗显着改变了 SARS-CoV2Δ 病毒载量和肺部特异性炎症。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 为了解决炎症细胞募集到肺部介导疾病的 CCR2 途径的功能相关性,每天在感染点给小鼠施用抗 CCR2 抗体,持续长达六天。

Immune-profiling by focused transcript analysis, inflammatory protein array, and multi-color flow cytometry, confirmed that clinically relevant markers of COVID-19 (IL-6, GM-CSF, neutrophils, inflammatory monocytes) were significantly elevated in lungs of mice at day 5 post-infection and that remdesivir anti-viral active metabolite (GS441524) treatment significantly modified SARS-CoV2Δ viral loads and pulmonary-specific inflammation. Chemokine ligands of CCR2 (CCL2/7/8) were amongst the top 5% upregulated pulmonary transcripts in a focused human infection response array to SARS-CoV2Δ. CCL2 was confirmed as elevated in protein assays in SARS-CoV2Δ infected lungs. To address functional relevance of the CCR2 pathway of inflammatory cell recruitment to the lungs mediating disease, mice were administered with anti-CCR2 antibody daily at point of infection for up to six days. Anti-CCR2 treated mice showed significant improved welfare scores, were protected from weight loss, modified myeloid pneumonitis, and displayed significantly blunted cytokine and chemokine response in the lungs, despite not affecting pulmonary viral loads. Our data supports therapeutic benefit of modifying CCR2-dependent cell recruitment in the treatment of viral-induced ARDS.

title: Herpesvirus reactivation is associated with mortality in critically ill ICU patients with COVID-19: Insights from a retrospective single-center analysis of 455 cases
abstract: BACKGROUND: Critically ill patients with COVID-19 frequently develop viral reactivation, yet the clinical significance of herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) and cytomegalovirus (CMV) remains a matter of debate. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-center study of 455 consecutive intensive care unit (ICU) patients with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection between March 2020 and December 2021. Patients underwent screening for HSV-1 and CMV in whole blood and respiratory samples. A multivariable model was used to independently investigate risk factors associated with mortality. RESULTS: The mean age was 57 years (range: 13-94 years), and 316 (69%) were male. During a median ICU stay of 14 (0-90) days, viral reactivation (either HSV-1 or CMV or both) occurred in 164 (36%) patients. HSV-1 and CMV co-reactivation was detected in 57 (13%) patients, isolated HSV-1 reactivation was observed in 54 (12%) patients and isolated CMV reactivation in 53 (12%) patients. Median time from ICU admission to viral detection was 4 days, with a stepwise increase with longer ICU stay. Detection of HSV-1 was associated with decreased ICU survival (32% versus 67%; p < 0.001) which remained significant after multivariable adjustment. Detection of HSV-1 but not CMV was associated with an increased need for invasive mechanical ventilation, veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation therapy, and the need for renal replacement therapy. Higher neutrophil-lymphocyte ratios were independently associated with an increased risk of ICU mortality and correlated with detection of HSV-1 and CMV. CONCLUSION: Herpesvirus reactivation was common in critically ill patients with COVID-19. HSV-1 reactivation was associated with a more severe course of disease and increased ICU mortality.

title: Durability and Breadth of Neutralizing Antibodies Against SARS-CoV-2 Variants Following XBB.1.5 Vaccination in a Multiply Exposed Cohort
abstract: Abstract Background Widespread immunity from vaccination and infection has reduced COVID-19 morbidity and mortality, but this immunity varies across the population. Understanding how repeated antigenic exposures influence antibody responses helps to inform future vaccination strategies. Methods We characterized neutralizing antibody responses in serum samples collected one and six months after XBB.1.5 vaccination from 25 healthcare workers with varying, complex histories of vaccination and reported infections. Neutralizing activity was assessed against a range of variants, from pre-Omicron to recent Omicron JN.1 sublineage, and divergent BA.3.2 variants using lentiviral pseudoviruses. Participants were stratified into five exposure groups based on their documented vaccination and reported infection history. Results XBB.1.5 vaccination elicited broad neutralizing responses, with strong boosting against previously encountered antigens relative to vaccine-matched XBB.1.5 and newer variants. Geometric mean neutralization titers were generally comparable across exposure groups, though small subgroup sizes and considerable intra-group heterogeneity precluded definitive conclusions about the influence of prior exposure history. At six months, titers declined by 36-62% across all variants. Titers remained highest against pre-Omicron variants and were lowest against JN.1 sublineage variants, with some falling to very low levels. Conclusions In this cohort with extensive prior antigenic exposures, broad neutralizing antibody profiles were observed following XBB.1.5 vaccination, though these responses waned substantially after six months. The observed waning of cross-neutralizing antibodies against emerging variants underscores the challenge of maintaining durable protection and supports the need for continued monitoring of antibody responses to guide evidence-based updates to COVID-19 vaccines.

title: Changes in mental health across gender and resilience among Norwegian adolescents into the COVID-19 pandemic: the Young-HUNT study.
abstract: Aims The objective of this follow-up study was to investigate whether changes in mental health from before and into the COVID-19 pandemic varied between girls and boys, as well as between adolescents with high and low levels of resilience. Methods We included data from Norwegian adolescents ( n = 1565, 64% girls) who participated in the Young-HUNT4 (2017-2019) and the Young-HUNT COVID (2021) surveys. We measured six dimensions of mental health using the Strength and Difficulties Questionnaire. The resilience factors-family cohesion, personal competence and social competence-were measured using the Resilience Scale for Adolescents. Linear mixed models were used to investigate whether change in the mental health dimensions depended on sex or level of resilience. Results Change in mental health appeared to differ by sex and resilience level. Specifically, girls showed greater increases in hyperactivity, emotional symptoms and total difficulties, whereas boys displayed greater increases in peer problems along with greater decreases in prosocial behaviour. Compared with adolescents with low resilience, those with high resilience demonstrated a stronger increase in emotional symptoms, peer problems and total difficulties. Adolescents with low resilience displayed a greater decrease in prosocial behaviour. A decrease in conduct problems was observed among adolescents with low resilience, which was not evident among those with high resilience. Conclusions The present findings suggest that girls and boys, as well as adolescents with high and low levels of resilience, may have experienced the pandemic situation somewhat differently.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated changes in mental health among Norwegian adolescents during the COVID-19 pandemic, comparing differences by sex and resilience levels. Using data from the Young-HUNT4 (2017-2019) and Young-HUNT COVID (2021) surveys, it measured six mental health dimensions and three resilience factors. Girls experienced greater increases in hyperactivity, emotional symptoms, and total difficulties, while boys showed larger increases in peer problems and decreases in prosocial behavior. elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,基于复原力的干预措施对于支持危机期间青少年的心理健康可能很重要,特别是对于女孩和复原力较低的人来说。

title: Institutional quality and pandemic resilience: cross-country evidence on health and economic outcomes during COVID-19.
abstract: Background The COVID-19 pandemic exposed large cross-country differences in mortality, vaccination rollout, and economic recovery. We examine whether stronger pre-pandemic institutions were associated with better pandemic performance and whether vaccination rollout helps explain part of that relationship. We combine 2019 World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators with COVID-19 outcomes, policy measures, World Development Indicators, and V-Dem electoral democracy data, estimating cross-country regressions and a temporally ordered exploratory mediation model using vaccination by September 2021 and deaths accrued in the fourth quarter of 2021. Results In full multivariable specifications, a one-unit increase in the WGI composite is associated with 384 fewer reported COVID-19 deaths per million, 1,860 fewer excess deaths per million, and 15.5% points higher full vaccination coverage by end-2021. These associations remain in robustness checks using V-Dem electoral democracy controls, WGI principal-component measures, timing-specific outcomes, and influence diagnostics. Institutional quality is not robustly associated with GDP growth in 2020; its positive association with GDP growth in 2021 persists but is weaker after controlling for OxCGRT economic-support policies. The exploratory mediation decomposition is consistent with an indirect path through vaccination representing about 35% of the total association between institutional quality and late-2021 mortality. Conclusions Pre-pandemic institutional quality was consistently associated with pandemic health outcomes and vaccine deployment, while economic associations were more phase-specific. The findings are observational and should not be read as definitive causal estimates, but they underscore the relevance of governance capacity for future pandemic preparedness.

title_zh: 机构质量和大流行抵御能力:关于 COVID-19 期间健康和经济结果的跨国证据。
source_body_en: Background The COVID-19 pandemic exposed large cross-country differences in mortality, vaccination rollout, and economic recovery. We examine whether stronger pre-pandemic institutions were associated with better pandemic performance and whether vaccination rollout helps explain part of that relationship. We combine 2019 World Bank Worldwide Governance Indicators with COVID-19 outcomes, policy measures, World Development Indicators, and V-Dem electoral democracy data, estimating cross-country regressions and a temporally ordered exploratory mediation model using vaccination by September 2021 and deaths accrued in the fourth quarter of 2021. Results In full multivariable specifications, a one-unit increase in the WGI composite is associated with 384 fewer reported COVID-19 deaths per million, 1,860 fewer excess deaths per million, and 15.5% points higher full vaccination coverage by end-2021. These associations remain in robustness checks using V-Dem electoral democracy controls, WGI principal-component measures, timing-specific outcomes, and influence diagnostics. Institutional quality is not robustly associated with GDP growth in 2020; its positive association with GDP growth in 2021 persists but is weaker after controlling for OxCGRT economic-support policies. The exploratory mediation decomposition is consistent with an indirect path through vaccination representing about 35% of the total association between institutional quality and late-2021 mortality. Conclusions Pre-pandemic institutional quality was consistently associated with pandemic health outcomes and vaccine deployment, while economic associations were more phase-specific. The findings are observational and should not be read as definitive causal estimates, but they underscore the relevance of governance capacity for future pandemic preparedness.
abstract_zh: 背景 COVID-19 大流行暴露了死亡率、疫苗接种推广和经济复苏方面的巨大跨国差异。我们研究了更强大的大流行前机构是否与更好的大流行表现相关,以及疫苗接种的推出是否有助于解释这种关系的部分原因。我们将 2019 年世界银行全球治理指标与 COVID-19 结果、政策措施、世界发展指标和 V-Dem 选举民主数据相结合,估计跨国回归和使用截至 2021 年 9 月疫苗接种的临时有序探索性调解模型以及 2021 年第四季度累计的死亡人数。结果在完整的多变量规范中,WGI 综合数据每增加一个单位,报告的死亡人数就会减少 384 人。到 2021 年底,每百万人的 COVID-19 死亡人数、每百万人的超额死亡人数减少 1,860 人,全面疫苗接种覆盖率提高 15.5%。使用 V-Dem 选举民主控制、WGI 主成分测量、特定时间结果和影响力诊断,对这些关联进行稳健性检查。制度质量与 2020 年 GDP 增长并不存在显着相关性;它与 2021 年 GDP 增长的正相关仍然存在,但在控制 OxCGRT 经济支持政策后,其正相关减弱。探索性中介分解与疫苗接种的间接路径一致,约占机构质量与 2021 年末死亡率之间总关联的 35%。结论 大流行前的机构质量始终与大流行健康结果和疫苗部署相关,而经济关联则更具阶段性。这些发现是观察性的,不应被解读为明确的因果估计,但它们强调了治理能力与未来大流行防范的相关性。

title: Clinical characteristics and predictors of severe pertussis in hospitalized children after the COVID-19 period in Türkiye: a multicenter study.
abstract: Pertussis resurged globally, after the relaxation of COVID-19 measures, underscoring its continued relevance as a public health concern, yet data remain limited on the factors associated with severe disease in children. The present study identified risk factors for severe pertussis to improve early recognition and clinical management. This multicenter retrospective study analyzed the demographic, clinical, and laboratory data of the 839 children hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed pertussis across 47 centers in Türkiye (2023-2024). Severe disease was defined as the need for respiratory support or the development of encephalopathy and/or cardiovascular dysfunction. After univariate comparison, significant variables were evaluated using center-adjusted multivariable logistic regression in vaccine-eligible (> 2 months) and non-eligible (≤ 2 months) groups. The patient's median age was 2 months (IQR 1.5-5.0), and 77.8% were younger than 6 months. Severe disease occurred in 26.1% of cases. In univariate analysis, younger age, vaccine refusal, refugee status, feeding difficulties, apnea, respiratory distress, leukocytosis, viral co-infection, and abnormal chest X-ray findings at admission were associated with severe disease. In infants ≤ 2 months, apnea (OR = 3.74; p 3 /μL increase; p = 0.003) were independently associated with severe disease. In children > 2 months, respiratory distress (OR = 13.59; p < 0.001) and not being up-to-date with vaccination (OR = 2.60; p = 0.019) were independent predictors of severe disease. Overall, 21.5% of patients required intensive care, 24.3% needed ventilation, and mortality was 2.4%. Conclusion: Severe pertussis predominantly affects young infants, and apnea, respiratory distress, and leukocytosis were identified as major predictors of severe disease. Furthermore, incomplete vaccination is associated with increased disease severity.

abstract_zh: 在放松 COVID-19 措施后,百日咳在全球范围内卷土重来,凸显了其作为公共卫生问题的持续相关性,但与儿童严重疾病相关的因素的数据仍然有限。本研究确定了严重百日咳的危险因素,以改善早期识别和临床管理。这项多中心回顾性研究分析了土耳其 47 个中心(2023-2024 年)因实验室确诊的百日咳住院的 839 名儿童的人口统计学、临床和实验室数据。严重疾病被定义为需要呼吸支持或发生脑病和/或心血管功能障碍。单变量比较后,使用中心调整的多变量逻辑回归在疫苗合格组(> 2个月)和不合格组(≤ 2个月)中评估显着变量。患者的中位年龄为2个月(IQR 1.5-5.0),77.8%小于6个月。26.1%的病例出现严重疾病。在单变量分析中,年龄较小、拒绝疫苗、难民身份、喂养困难、呼吸暂停、呼吸窘迫、白细胞增多、病毒合并感染和入院时胸部 X 光检查结果异常与严重疾病相关。在 ≤ 2 个月的婴儿中,呼吸暂停(OR = 3.74;p 3 /μL 增加;p = 0.003)与严重疾病独立相关。在大于 2 个月的儿童中,呼吸窘迫(OR = 13.59;p < 0.001)和未及时接种疫苗(OR = 2.60;p = 0.019)是严重疾病的独立预测因素。总体而言,21.5% 的患者需要重症监护,24.3% 需要通气,死亡率为 2.4%。结论:重症百日咳主要影响小婴儿,呼吸暂停、呼吸窘迫和白细胞增多被认为是重症百日咳的主要预测因素。此外,不完整的疫苗接种与疾病严重程度的增加有关。

title: Generation and immunological evaluation of SARS-CoV-2 membrane protein virus-like particles
abstract: BACKGROUND: The emergence of the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic led to the spread of highly transmissible variants, such as the Delta variant, which originated in India, underscoring the urgent need to develop new antivirals, therapeutics, and vaccines. In our previous study, we showed that Membrane-Envelope Virus-like Particles exhibit antigenicity and neutralization activity. Hence, our present study was conducted to evaluate whether the M protein alone can form VLPs that elicit an immune response. METHODS: Using computational methods, we identified key interacting residues in M-protein that contribute to VLP formation and interact with other structural proteins, including Spike (S), Nucleocapsid (N), and Envelope (E). The SARS-CoV-2-M protein was expressed in Sf-21 insect cells, and the resulting VLPs were purified, analyzed for shape and size, and characterized using DLS, FESEM, and TEM. The purified VLPs were injected into BALB/c mice to evaluate their immune response compared with uninfected controls. RESULTS: The biophysical analysis confirms that the particles are round and have a size of ~ 180-200 nm. The serum levels of IgG, IgM, and IgA were found to be higher in immunized mice than in uninfected mice. Further qRT-PCR analysis demonstrated the levels of IFN-γ, IL-2, and IL-12, indicating a TH1-biased immune response against the M protein. CONCLUSION: Our study demonstrates that the highly conserved M protein can self-assemble into VLPs and elicit humoral and cellular immune response. Furthermore, our study indicates that while M-protein VLPs elicit significant antibodies and cytokine responses, they do not induce detectable neutralizing activity when given alone.

abstract_zh: 背景:SARS-CoV-2大流行的出现导致了高传染性变种的传播,例如起源于印度的Delta变种,这凸显了开发新的抗病毒药物、治疗方法和疫苗的迫切需要。在我们之前的研究中,我们表明膜包膜病毒样颗粒表现出抗原性和中和活性。因此,我们目前的研究旨在评估单独的 M 蛋白是否可以形成引发免疫反应的 VLP。方法:使用计算方法,我们确定了 M 蛋白中有助于 VLP 形成并与其他结构蛋白相互作用的关键相互作用残基,包括刺突 (S)、核衣壳 (N) 和包膜 (E)。SARS-CoV-2-M 蛋白在 Sf-21 昆虫细胞中表达,所得的 VLP 经纯化、形状和大小分析,并使用 DLS、FESEM 和 TEM 进行表征。将纯化的 VLP 注射到 BALB/c 小鼠中,以与未感染的对照小鼠相比评估其免疫反应。结果:生物物理分析证实颗粒呈圆形,尺寸约为 180-200 nm。研究发现,免疫小鼠的血清 IgG、IgM 和 IgA 水平高于未感染小鼠。进一步的 qRT-PCR 分析显示了 IFN-γ、IL-2 和 IL-12 的水平,表明针对 M 蛋白的 TH1 偏向免疫反应。结论:我们的研究表明,高度保守的 M 蛋白可以自组装成 VLP,并引发体液和细胞免疫反应。此外,我们的研究表明,虽然 M 蛋白 VLP 引发显着的抗体和细胞因子反应,但单独给予时,它们不会诱导可检测的中和活性。

title: COVID-19 and temporal perception: prolonged short-term time perception in a post-pandemic world
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly restructured daily life, significantly impacting mental health. This negative event has been reported to alter subjective experience of time, such as the blending of days, reflecting distortions in long-term time perception over relatively coarse scales. However, the influence of the COVID-19 pandemic on short-term time perception over fine scales has received much less attention. Here we delve into this underexplored territory, demonstrating that the pandemic, as a high-arousal negative event, lengthens our perception of short time intervals. Using a two-session duration discrimination paradigm, we showed that COVID-19 related images were perceived as significantly longer than neutral pictures of the same duration. Unlike emotion-induced temporal distortions, this dilation was consistent across sessions, correlated with heightened arousal, remained unaffected by anxiety, and exhibited a long-lasting effect - persisting even four years after the initial outbreak. Taken together, our findings highlight a temporal dilation induced by COVID-19 stimuli, extending our understanding of how high-arousal negative events interact with cognitive processes, particularly time perception.

abstract_zh: COVID-19 大流行深刻地改变了日常生活,极大地影响了心理健康。据报道,这种负面事件会改变对时间的主观体验,例如日期的混合,反映了相对粗糙尺度上长期时间感知的扭曲。然而,COVID-19 大流行对细尺度短期时间感知的影响却很少受到关注。在这里,我们深入研究了这个尚未充分探索的领域,证明大流行作为一种高度唤醒的负面事件,延长了我们对短时间间隔的感知。使用两个会话持续时间歧视范式,我们发现与 COVID-19 相关的图像被感知为明显长于相同持续时间的中性图片。与情绪引起的时间扭曲不同,这种扩张在整个过程中是一致的,与高度的唤醒相关,不受焦虑的影响,并且表现出持久的影响——甚至在最初爆发四年后仍然存在。总而言之,我们的研究结果强调了 COVID-19 刺激引起的时间扩张,扩展了我们对高唤醒负面事件如何与认知过程(特别是时间感知)相互作用的理解。

title: The Resurgence of Respiratory Viruses After COVID-19: Molecular Insights from Pediatric SARI in Kashmir.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are major contributors to severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) in children. Data on their molecular epidemiology in northern India remains limited, particularly in the post-COVID-19 period. This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of respiratory viral pathogens among hospitalized pediatric SARI patients in Kashmir. METHODS: A prospective study was conducted from October 2023 to April 2025 at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar. Children aged ≤15 years meeting the World Health Organization SARI case definition were enrolled. Nasopharyngeal and/or oropharyngeal samples were collected and tested using real-time polymerase chain reaction assays for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B, Respiratory Syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, Adenovirus, Human metapneumovirus, Rhinovirus, and Para-influenza viruses. RESULTS: A total of 326 pediatric SARI cases were included. At least one respiratory virus was detected in 200 patients (61.3%). RSV was the most frequently detected virus, with RSV-B identified in 111 cases (34.0%) and RSV-A in 26 cases (7.9%). Influenza viruses accounted for a smaller proportion, including influenza A(H1N1) in 12 cases (3.6%), influenza A(H3N2) in 6 cases (1.8%), and influenza B (Victoria lineage) in 21 cases (6.4%). Other viruses detected included Adenovirus, Para-influenza virus, Rhinovirus, and Human metapneumovirus. Most infections occurred during winter months and predominantly affected infants. CONCLUSION: Respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of pediatric SARI cases in Kashmir, with RSV emerging as the predominant pathogen in the post-pandemic period. Strengthening molecular surveillance may improve diagnostic stewardship and guide targeted prevention strategies.

This study aimed to determine the prevalence and distribution of respiratory viral pathogens among hospitalized pediatric SARI patients in Kashmir. Methods A prospective study was conducted from October 2023 to April 2025 at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences, Srinagar. Children aged ≤15 years meeting the World Health Organization SARI case definition were enrolled. Nasopharyngeal and/or oropharyngeal samples were collected and tested using real-time polymerase chain reaction assays for SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and B, Respiratory Syncytial virus (RSV) A and B, Adenovirus, Human metapneumovirus, Rhinovirus, and Para-influenza viruses. Results A total of 326 pediatric SARI cases were included. At least one respiratory virus was detected in 200 patients (61.3%). RSV was the most frequently detected virus, with RSV-B identified in 111 cases (34.0%) and RSV-A in 26 cases (7.9%). Influenza viruses accounted for a smaller proportion, including influenza A(H1N1) in 12 cases (3.6%), influenza A(H3N2) in 6 cases (1.8%), and influenza B (Victoria lineage) in 21 cases (6.4%). Other viruses detected included Adenovirus, Para-influenza virus, Rhinovirus, and Human metapneumovirus. Most infections occurred during winter months and predominantly affected infants. Conclusion Respiratory viruses account for a substantial proportion of pediatric SARI cases in Kashmir, with RSV emerging as the predominant pathogen in the post-pandemic period. Strengthening molecular surveillance may improve diagnostic stewardship and guide targeted prevention strategies.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective study from October 2023 to April 2025 at a tertiary care centre in Kashmir investigated the molecular epidemiology of respiratory viruses among 326 hospitalized pediatric SARI cases aged ≤15 years. Using RT-PCR assays, at least one respiratory virus was detected in 61.3% of cases, with RSV (34.0% RSV-B, 7.9% RSV-A) being the most prevalent, followed by influenza viruses (3.6% A(H1N1), 1.8% A(H3N2), 6.4% B Victoria lineage). title: Global Viral Lower Respiratory Disease Episodes, Hospitalisations, and Clinical Outcomes by Aetiology, 2010–2021
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Viral lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) is a major cause of global morbidity and mortality, but pathogen-specific estimates remain limited. We aimed to quantify the global burden of viral LRTD episodes, hospitalisations, and severe clinical outcomes by aetiology from 2010 to 2021. METHODS: We used the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 modelling framework to generate estimates of viral LRTD incidence, hospitalisations, and clinical outcomes from 2010 to 2021 for 204 countries and territories, 21 regions, and seven super-regions. Aetiology-specific estimates were generated for five viral categories: influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), SARS-CoV-2, and "other" viral pathogens. Data inputs included surveillance systems, clinical informatics, published literature, surveys, and vital registration. Viral LRTD incidence was estimated using DisMod-MR 2.1, a GBD Bayesian meta-regression tool for disease incidence. We then applied location-specific admission scalars, adjusted for healthcare access, to derive hospitalisations. Aetiology-specific clinical outcome proportions-including intensive care unit (ICU) need, invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) need, and in-hospital mortality-were estimated using meta-regression-Bayesian, regularised, trimming models. These were then applied to the hospitalisation estimates. COVID-19 incidence and hospitalisations were estimated using established GBD COVID-19 methods. All estimates are reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). RESULTS: Globally, viral LRTD episodes increased from 82.3 million (95% UI 76.4-88.2) in 2010 to 94.9 million (88.8-101.2) in 2019, while episode rates remained relatively stable at approximately 1200 per 100,000 population. Over the same period, hospitalisation rates increased by 40%, from 103.7 (96.1-111.4) to 145.4 (134.6-156.4) per 100,000 population. In 2020 and 2021, the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 resulted in sharp increases in burden, with episodes exceeding 1.1 billion in 2020 and 1.5 billion in 2021. During this period, 2020-2021, episode and hospitalisation rates associated with influenza, RSV, and hMPV declined by nearly 50%. Between 2010 and 2019, global rates of ICU need increased from 16.1 (14.3-18.0) to 23.7 (21.0-26.6) per 100,000 population, IMV need from 7.5 (6.7-8.4) to 11.2 (10.0-12.6), and in-hospital mortality from 9.4 (8.4-10.5) to 13.9 (12.3-15.6). In 2020-2021, SARS-CoV-2 dominated severe outcomes, with in-hospital mortality reaching 87.7 (83.3-92.2) per 100,000 population in 2021. Across the study period, older adults consistently experienced the highest rates of severe outcomes, and substantial regional variation was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Before 2020, global incidence of viral LRTD was stable; however, hospitalisations and severe outcomes increased substantially, suggesting rising clinical severity and healthcare demand. The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered the global viral LRTD landscape, driving unprecedented increases in hospitalisations, intensive care use, and mortality, while suppressing other respiratory viruses in the years 2020 and 2021. These findings demonstrate a substantial burden of severe viral LRTD globally, with marked age and regional variations, underscoring the importance of sustained aetiology-specific surveillance, adequate healthcare capacity, and equitable access to preventive and therapeutic interventions.

METHODS We used the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 modelling framework to generate estimates of viral LRTD incidence, hospitalisations, and clinical outcomes from 2010 to 2021 for 204 countries and territories, 21 regions, and seven super-regions. Aetiology-specific estimates were generated for five viral categories: influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus (hMPV), SARS-CoV-2, and "other" viral pathogens. Data inputs included surveillance systems, clinical informatics, published literature, surveys, and vital registration. Viral LRTD incidence was estimated using DisMod-MR 2.1, a GBD Bayesian meta-regression tool for disease incidence. We then applied location-specific admission scalars, adjusted for healthcare access, to derive hospitalisations. Aetiology-specific clinical outcome proportions-including intensive care unit (ICU) need, invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) need, and in-hospital mortality-were estimated using meta-regression-Bayesian, regularised, trimming models. These were then applied to the hospitalisation estimates. COVID-19 incidence and hospitalisations were estimated using established GBD COVID-19 methods. All estimates are reported with 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs). RESULTS Globally, viral LRTD episodes increased from 82.3 million (95% UI 76.4-88.2) in 2010 to 94.9 million (88.8-101.2) in 2019, while episode rates remained relatively stable at approximately 1200 per 100,000 population. Over the same period, hospitalisation rates increased by 40%, from 103.7 (96.1-111.4) to 145.4 (134.6-156.4) per 100,000 population. In 2020 and 2021, the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 resulted in sharp increases in burden, with episodes exceeding 1.1 billion in 2020 and 1.5 billion in 2021. During this period, 2020-2021, episode and hospitalisation rates associated with influenza, RSV, and hMPV declined by nearly 50%. Between 2010 and 2019, global rates of ICU need increased from 16.1 (14.3-18.0) to 23.7 (21.0-26.6) per 100,000 population, IMV need from 7.5 (6.7-8.4) to 11.2 (10.0-12.6), and in-hospital mortality from 9.4 (8.4-10.5) to 13.9 (12.3-15.6). In 2020-2021, SARS-CoV-2 dominated severe outcomes, with in-hospital mortality reaching 87.7 (83.3-92.2) per 100,000 population in 2021. Across the study period, older adults consistently experienced the highest rates of severe outcomes, and substantial regional variation was observed. CONCLUSIONS Before 2020, global incidence of viral LRTD was stable; however, hospitalisations and severe outcomes increased substantially, suggesting rising clinical severity and healthcare demand. The COVID-19 pandemic profoundly altered the global viral LRTD landscape, driving unprecedented increases in hospitalisations, intensive care use, and mortality, while suppressing other respiratory viruses in the years 2020 and 2021. These findings demonstrate a substantial burden of severe viral LRTD globally, with marked age and regional variations, underscoring the importance of sustained aetiology-specific surveillance, adequate healthcare capacity, and equitable access to preventive and therapeutic interventions.

title: Identifying severe COVID-19 risk variants modulating enhancer reporter activity in lung cells
abstract: Common genetic variants contribute to risk for complex human diseases. However, despite thousands of associations, variants modulating disease risk and their functional impact remain largely unknown. This includes SARS-CoV-2 infection, where outcomes range from asymptomatic to fatal. Most genetic risk variants associated with COVID-19 disease, identified through genome wide association studies, are located in the non-coding genome and may function by altering gene expression in disease-relevant cells and tissues. To address this at scale, we tested >4800 severe COVID-19-associated variants to determine the impact of individual variants and variant combinations on regulatory activity using Self-Transcribing Active Regulatory Region sequencing, a massively-parallel reporter assay. Focusing on variants that may have their impact in the lung, in a lung epithelial cell line (A549) we identify 166 variants within active sequences, of which 29 modulate activity allele-specifically. Evaluating variant combinations, we observe both additive and non-additive effects on regulatory activity. We employ state-of-the-art deep learning models to interpret allele-specific variant effects on regulatory activity and endogenous genomic features. Our work provides a set of prioritised severe COVID-19-associated variants that modulate regulatory activity in lung epithelial cells, candidate transcription factors, and candidate target genes with potential to be disease modifying.

title_zh: 识别调节肺细胞增强子报告活性的严重 COVID-19 风险变异
source_body_en: Common genetic variants contribute to risk for complex human diseases. However, despite thousands of associations, variants modulating disease risk and their functional impact remain largely unknown. This includes SARS-CoV-2 infection, where outcomes range from asymptomatic to fatal. Most genetic risk variants associated with COVID-19 disease, identified through genome wide association studies, are located in the non-coding genome and may function by altering gene expression in disease-relevant cells and tissues. To address this at scale, we tested >4800 severe COVID-19-associated variants to determine the impact of individual variants and variant combinations on regulatory activity using Self-Transcribing Active Regulatory Region sequencing, a massively-parallel reporter assay. Focusing on variants that may have their impact in the lung, in a lung epithelial cell line (A549) we identify 166 variants within active sequences, of which 29 modulate activity allele-specifically. Evaluating variant combinations, we observe both additive and non-additive effects on regulatory activity. We employ state-of-the-art deep learning models to interpret allele-specific variant effects on regulatory activity and endogenous genomic features. Our work provides a set of prioritised severe COVID-19-associated variants that modulate regulatory activity in lung epithelial cells, candidate transcription factors, and candidate target genes with potential to be disease modifying.
abstract_zh: 常见的遗传变异会增加复杂人类疾病的风险。然而,尽管存在数千种关联,但调节疾病风险的变异及其功能影响仍然很大程度上未知。这包括 SARS-CoV-2 感染,其后果从无症状到致命不等。通过全基因组关联研究鉴定出的大多数与 COVID-19 疾病相关的遗传风险变异位于非编码基因组中,可能通过改变疾病相关细胞和组织中的基因表达来发挥作用。为了大规模解决这个问题,我们使用自转录活性调节区测序(一种大规模并行报告分析)测试了超过 4800 个严重的 COVID-19 相关变异,以确定单个变异和变异组合对监管活动的影响。着眼于可能对肺产生影响的变异,在肺上皮细胞系 (A549) 中,我们鉴定了活性序列内的 166 个变异,其中 29 个特异性调节等位基因活性。通过评估变体组合,我们观察到对监管活动的加性和非加性影响。我们采用最先进的深度学习模型来解释等位基因特异性变异对调控活动和内源基因组特征的影响。我们的工作提供了一组优先的严重 COVID-19 相关变体,这些变体调节肺上皮细胞、候选转录因子和候选靶基因的调节活性,有可能改变疾病。

title: Covid-19 related excess mortality: An analysis by age for selected countries
abstract: BACKGROUND: Measures of excess mortality are generally regarded as providing the best metric for countries' experience during the Covid pandemic of 2020-2022. Such measures, however, need to be adjusted to take account of the different age structures of different countries as Covid-related mortality can differ substantially by age. METHODS: This paper analyses excess mortality data for a selection of countries using the Short Term Mortality Fluctuations dataset. A standardised age distribution is applied to the data to obtain age-adjusted excess mortality and this is compared to crude excess mortality data. The metric of years of life lost (YLL) is also calculated for the same dataset and cluster analysis is applied to investigate relationships between the mortality metrics and GDP per capita and inequality. RESULTS: The age adjustment makes a significant difference for some countries but the overall ranking of countries in terms of excess mortality changes very little, with rank correlation coefficients in excess of 0.95 for the metrics of crude mortality, age adjusted mortality and YLL Age adjusted excess mortality has a rank correlation of -0.69 with GDP per capita but the rank correlation with the Gini coefficient of 0.11 is not statistically significant. CONCLUSIONS: Rankings of countries by excess mortality during the Covid period are robust to age adjustment and choice of mortality metric. Cluster analysis suggests distinct clusterings of countries with similar outcomes, particularly the former planned economies of central and eastern Europe.
